Paper title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale
Primary contribution: Introduces patch-embedding sequence with class token and pure Transformer image encoder; reference architecture for the visual tower, not a multimodal compressor.
Training methodology: Supervised pretraining on ImageNet-1k, ImageNet-21k or JFT-300M; task-specific finetuning, with higher image resolution on major ImageNet comparison.
Compression mechanism: Patchification and global self-attention; optional CNN hybrid; 2D interpolation of positions for higher-resolution transfer.
Relevance to our proposal: Backbone context; patch-token generation and encoder compute constrain where to intervene.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Use as the fixed-token baseline and initialization substrate; no direct answer to question-conditioned dynamic budget.
Method evidence (PDF pages): Section 3.1 PDF pp.3–4 (equations 1–4, patch count and CLS); Section 3.2 PDF p.4 (position interpolation).
Experimental evidence (PDF pages): Sections 4.1–4.2 PDF pp.4–6, especially Tables 1–2 PDF pp.5–6.
Question conditioning: None: image classification has no question/text input.
Adaptive budget: No adaptive token budgeting; patch size/resolution fixed by model and finetuning configuration.
Frozen components: No frozen language decoder. ViT pretrained and subsequently finetuned; frozen features only in optional few-shot evaluation.
Training objective: Supervised image-label classification cross-entropy; finetuning downstream; no compute-aware objective or RL.
Benchmarks: ImageNet; ImageNet ReaL; CIFAR-10; CIFAR-100; Oxford-IIIT Pets; Oxford Flowers-102; VTAB-1k
Reported results: ViT-H/14 pretrained JFT-300M: ImageNet 88.55±0.04%, CIFAR-100 94.55±0.04%, VTAB 77.63±0.23%; 2.5k TPUv3-core-days (Table 2, PDF p.6).; ViT-L/16 JFT-300M: ImageNet 87.76±0.03%, VTAB 76.28±0.46%; 0.68k TPUv3-core-days (Table 2, PDF p.6).
Limitations: Needs large-scale pretraining for strong performance; self-attention cost and sequence count grow with finer patches/higher resolution; no text alignment or adaptive compression.
Warnings: Filename starts 2020 (original arXiv identifier 2010.11929) but examined PDF is published ICLR 2021; year set to publication year.

Paper title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision
Primary contribution: CLIP trains paired image/text encoders with symmetric image-text contrastive objective; enables prompt-driven zero-shot classification; useful source of aligned features, not a token controller.
Training methodology: Image and text encoders trained jointly from scratch on 400M web image-text pairs (WIT), 32 epochs, batch 32,768; zero-shot uses text templates and normalized similarities.
Compression mechanism: Pairwise cosine matrix, symmetric image-to-text and text-to-image softmax cross-entropy over batch; prompt templates/ensemble at inference.
Relevance to our proposal: Provides pretrained vision/text alignment and semantic similarity as a signal for question-guided policy.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Alignment prior, but no learned variable-length compressor or frozen generative decoder.
Method evidence (PDF pages): Sections 2.3–2.5 PDF pp.4–5 (Figure 3 loss and encoder designs); Section 3.1.2 PDF p.6 (prompt-based zero-shot).
Experimental evidence (PDF pages): Section 3 and Figure 5 PDF pp.6–9; limitations discussion PDF pp.20–21.
Question conditioning: Text prompts select class embeddings for zero-shot decisions, but do not condition selection of image patch tokens.
Adaptive budget: No adaptive budget; preset encoder resolution/patch size and model variant.
Frozen components: No frozen decoder; both encoders trained for CLIP. Frozen embeddings used for zero-shot inference/linear probe only.
Training objective: Bidirectional contrastive cross-entropy on matched versus in-batch mismatched image-text pairs; no compute/token penalty.
Benchmarks: ImageNet zero-shot; 27-dataset zero-shot suite; image-text retrieval; ImageNet distribution shift
Reported results: Zero-shot CLIP outperforms supervised linear classifier on ResNet-50 features on 16/27 evaluated datasets (Figure 5, PDF p.8).; Prompt ensembling uses 80 context templates for ImageNet (Section 3.1, PDF p.8).
Limitations: Global image/text alignment rather than per-question patch relevance; zero-shot prompt engineering uses validation feedback, noted as a methodological limitation in paper; model has no generation decoder.

Paper title: DynamicViT: Efficient Vision Transformers with Dynamic Token Sparsification
Research category: Token pruning and merging; Supervised and differentiable compression
Primary contribution: Hierarchical learned sample-dependent token pruning within ViT; Gumbel-Softmax and masking allow end-to-end training with accuracy/distillation/target-ratio losses.
Training methodology: Initialize pretrained DeiT/LV-ViT; jointly train predictor and backbone 30 epochs, with backbone frozen only first 5 epochs and then 0.01× predictor learning rate.
Compression mechanism: Local token MLP plus global retained-token average; drop/keep probabilities; training Gumbel-Softmax binary decisions and attention mask; inference top-k by keep probability.
Relevance to our proposal: Direct precedent for learned visual routing and ratio/distillation penalties; question input and per-question count would extend it.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Important distinction: image-conditional selection is not count-adaptive; full-frozen-decoder transfer requires new design.
Method evidence (PDF pages): Sections 3.1–3.4 PDF pp.3–6, especially Eqs.1–17 and teacher/freeze schedule.
Question conditioning: None: predictor sees visual token features/global visual average but no question or text.
Adaptive budget: Visual token identities depend on each image, but inference enforces exact predefined per-stage counts floor(ρ^sN); not example-wise variable token count.
Frozen components: Original backbone is teacher for distillation, but student backbone not kept frozen throughout. No LLM decoder.
Training objective: L = classification cross entropy +0.5 teacher-output KL +0.5 token-feature distillation +2 target-stage keep-ratio MSE (Eq.16); fixed ratio rather than latency reward.
Benchmarks: ImageNet-1k classification
Reported results: DeiT-S, ρ=0.7: 79.3% top-1 vs 79.8% original, 2.9 vs 4.6 GFLOPs, 2062.1 vs 1337.7 images/s on RTX 3090 batch 32 (Table 1, PDF p.6).; At 2.9 GFLOPs, dynamic 79.3%, static 73.4%, structural 78.2% (Table 4, PDF p.10).
Limitations: Only image classification; downstream VQA/generative faithfulness untested. Inference ratio fixed per stage; training keeps padded full shape under masking, so no actual train-time token-length savings.

Paper title: Sigmoid Loss for Language Image Pre-Training
Primary contribution: Replaces batch-normalized softmax contrastive loss by pairwise sigmoid/logistic loss for image-text alignment; relevant as source of text/vision features, not a pruning policy.
Training methodology: SigLIP trains image/text encoders jointly (from scratch or pretrained image init); SigLiT uses frozen image encoder and trains text; batch sizes up to one million studied, 32k sufficient in reported settings.
Compression mechanism: For all image-text pairs in batch, y=+1 for matched, −1 otherwise; sigmoid loss −sum logσ(y×(cosine×temperature+bias))/N; supports chunked pair computation.
Relevance to our proposal: Pretrained multimodal alignment features for routing; SigLIP text tower is directly used by AdaptMerge.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Not a direct compressor; could supply reward or relevance scores but those are separate designs.
Method evidence (PDF pages): Section 3/Algorithm 1 PDF pp.2–3; Sec.4.1 PDF p.4 (batch scaling).
Experimental evidence (PDF pages): Sections 4.1–4.10 PDF pp.4–9, Table 1 PDF p.1, Table 3 PDF p.8.
Question conditioning: Text paired with images trains representation alignment; no task-question-to-patch selection.
Adaptive budget: No input-adaptive visual token budget; batch-size scaling is training batch size, not visual token budgeting.
Frozen components: SigLiT locks image tower; SigLIP generally does not. No frozen generative decoder.
Training objective: Pairwise sigmoid binary classification across positive/negative image-text pairs, with learned bias/temperature; no token count/compute objective.
Benchmarks: ImageNet zero-shot; COCO image-text retrieval; XM3600 multilingual retrieval; ImageNet-v2; ObjectNet
Reported results: SigLiT frozen g/14 image encoder 84.5% ImageNet zero-shot after 2 days on 4 TPU-v4 chips (Table 1, PDF p.1).; SigLIP L with 576 image patches: ImageNet-1k zero-shot 82.1%, COCO image-to-text R@1 70.6 and text-to-image R@1 52.7 (Table 3, PDF p.8).; Batch-size performance saturates near 32k in studied configurations (Figure 2, PDF p.4).
Limitations: Global similarity objective does not directly optimize image regions or question-conditioned visual budget; one-million batch size is not one-million visual tokens.

Paper title: Token Merging: Your ViT But Faster
Primary contribution: ToMe merges similar tokens progressively inside pretrained ViTs using fast bipartite soft matching, often without retraining.
Training methodology: Off-the-shelf insertion requires no training; optional training from scratch or finetuning with merging as pooling operation.
Compression mechanism: Alternating two-way token partition, nearest-match edges, choose r strongest, size-weighted average merging; key cosine, size-aware proportional attention.
Relevance to our proposal: Strong visual merging baseline; separates similarity-preserving merge from relevance-aware variable-budget compression.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Compare against ToMe at matched latency; novelty is not simply merging existing pretrained vision tokens.
Method evidence (PDF pages): Section 3 PDF pp.2–4 (Figure 1, bipartite matching, Eq.1 proportional attention); Appendix D PDF p.18 implementation.
Experimental evidence (PDF pages): Sections 4.1–4.3 PDF pp.4–7, Tables 1–4; Sections 5–6 PDF pp.8–9.
Question conditioning: None; no text/query representation used for matching.
Adaptive budget: Constant predetermined r merges per layer/default schedule; pairs depend on image features, output count not adaptively allocated per question.
Frozen components: None frozen by design in training-free setup (all existing weights untouched); optional retraining updates ViT. No generative decoder.
Training objective: No new loss when used off-the-shelf; optional standard task-specific training loss; no explicit compute-budget/RL reward.
Benchmarks: ImageNet-1k classification; video classification; audio classification
Reported results: Untrained MAE ViT-L/16 r=8: 84.25% ImageNet top-1 at 182.9 im/s versus 85.96% at 93.3 im/s baseline on V100 fp32 (Table 1, PDF p.4).; ToMe DeiT-S trained from scratch: 79.4% accuracy, 2.7 GFLOPs, 1552 im/s versus DynamicViT 79.3%, 2.9 GFLOPs, 1505 im/s in their V100 comparison (Table 4, PDF p.7).; On large SWAG ViT-L/512 and ViT-H/518, off-the-shelf ~2× throughput with ~0.3% top-1 accuracy drop (Section 4.2, PDF p.6).
Limitations: Fixed reduction schedule; no query grounding or generative VQA evaluation; aggressive merging can lose fine details; batch shape convenience is partly a consequence of constant r.

Paper title: Patch Ranking: Token Pruning as Ranking Prediction for Efficient CLIP
Research category: Token pruning and merging; Supervised and differentiable compression
Primary contribution: Three-stage CLIP ViT patch-pruning method: derive costly oracle/golden rankings from task/embedding impact, train early-layer predictor, optionally tune visual/text prompt tokens to recover quality.
Training methodology: Compute-intensive offline teacher ranking; predictor and optional 16 visual/16 text prompt tokens trained; pretrained CLIP backbones depicted frozen during prompt tuning.
Compression mechanism: Sliding r×r removal-window evaluation against label-confidence, max-confidence or CLS-feature-preservation oracle; predictor approximates normalized oracle scores then prunes low-score patches; optional learned prompts.
Relevance to our proposal: Important precedent for learned importance prediction from expensive task-conditioned oracle with pretrained vision backbone.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Text class prompts in oracle do not mean the deployment policy is conditioned on arbitrary question; novelty must explicitly articulate this and per-instance budget.
Method evidence (PDF pages): Sections 3.1–3.3 PDF pp.3–5, especially Eq.8 and inference fixed-count sentence PDF p.4.
Experimental evidence (PDF pages): Section 4 PDF pp.5–8, Tables 2–5 PDF pp.7–8.
Question conditioning: Training golden-ranking classification scores depend on text class prompts/labels; runtime predictor takes visual features Z^(i), not a free-form user question. Optional text prompt tuning is task templates, not per-question routing.
Adaptive budget: Fixed preselected pruning count/keep rate per setting, e.g. 20 tokens at each selected block, not per-question variable budget.
Frozen components: CLIP image/text encoder weights frozen in prompt-tuning diagram PDF p.3; predictor/prompts trained. No LLM decoder.
Training objective: Oracle scores use label-class probability, max-class probability, or CLS cosine preservation; predictor minimizes sigmoid-transformed golden-score cross-entropy in Eq.8; prompt tuning uses task classification, no compute/RL term.
Benchmarks: Caltech101; OxfordPets; Flowers102; Food101; FGVCAircraft; DTD; UCF101; ImageNet
Reported results: At 16.8 GFLOPs (vs full CLIP 23.4), eight-dataset average 65.4% for pruning-only method versus EViT 64.3%, A-ViT 63.8%, ToMe 64.2% (Table 4, PDF p.8).; Seven-dataset average: no pruning 67.9%, pruning alone 66.3%; text+visual prompt tuning 79.8% without pruning vs 79.5% with pruning (Table 5, PDF p.8).; CLIP at 60% keep: 23.4→16.8 GFLOPs and reported latency 3.5→1.6 ms (Table 3, PDF p.7).
Limitations: Full-sequence repeated forward passes needed to create golden ranking offline; class-label oracle unavailable at test; evaluated predominantly CLIP zero-shot classification rather than autoregressive question answering.
Warnings: Filename labels 2025 but examined PDF identifies arXiv:2409.14607v2 dated November 28, 2024; year set to document version year, venue year not verified.; PDF page text in math equations includes literal LaTeX extraction artifacts; interpretation checked against adjacent prose.

Paper title: SigLIP 2: Multilingual Vision-Language Encoders with Improved Semantic Understanding, Localization, and Dense Features
Primary contribution: Improves SigLIP through joint image-text sigmoid and caption/localization objectives, late self-distillation and masked-patch prediction; NaFlex permits native aspect ratio and preset variable max sequence lengths.
Training methodology: WebLI image-text training (109 languages; 90% English /10% others), 32k batch, 40B seen examples; self-distillation/masked prediction introduced at 80% progress, resolution variants resumed late.
Compression mechanism: Staged sigmoid image-text alignment + LocCa caption/referring expression and grounded captions; late teacher-student local-global and masked-token feature matching; NaFlex resizing/positional interpolation.
Relevance to our proposal: Strong swappable vision/text feature pair; NaFlex important static/shape-conditioned budget baseline and OCR/detail caveat.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Need distinguish aspect-ratio/target-length flexibility from true question-conditional learned budgets.
Method evidence (PDF pages): Sections 2.1–2.4.2 PDF pp.2–4 (Figure 1; loss staging; NaFlex max target length).
Experimental evidence (PDF pages): Section 3 PDF pp.5–11, Tables 1–3 PDF pp.5,9–11 and Figure 3 PDF p.7.
Question conditioning: Text informs image-text pretraining and auxiliary captioning; no prompt-aware patch routing at inference.
Adaptive budget: NaFlex has user-chosen target length/resolution and natural aspect-dependent padding; variable across image shapes, not learned per-question optimal budget.
Frozen components: Image/text pretrained jointly; EMA teacher stop-gradient; auxiliary training-only decoder omitted from released checkpoints. This is not a frozen pretrained generative LLM.
Training objective: Equal-weight SigLIP sigmoid and LocCa decoder loss; late local-global consistency and masked prediction loss, scaled by model size; no compute-aware downstream answer reward.
Benchmarks: ImageNet zero-shot; COCO/Flickr/XM3600 retrieval; AI2D; DocVQA; PASCAL/ADE20k segmentation; NYUv2 depth; RefCOCO localization
Reported results: B/16 224px 196 tokens: ImageNet zero-shot 78.2% versus SigLIP 76.2%; COCO text-to-image R@1 52.1 versus 47.2 (Table 1, PDF p.5).; So/14 384px frozen-feature ADE20k mIoU 45.4 versus SigLIP 40.8 (Table 2, PDF p.9).; B encoder 256 tokens RefCOCO val 83.76 versus SigLIP 64.05 (PDF p.11).
Limitations: Changing resolution/length can discard detail, but no policy for question-driven compute allocation or frozen-decoder generative VQA; decoder used for pretraining and not released.

Paper title: AdaptMerge: Inference Time Adaptive Visual and Language-Guided Token Merging for Efficient Large Multimodal Models
Research category: Adaptive visual token compression; Question-conditioned vision encoding; Token pruning and merging
Primary contribution: Training-free adaptive variable-length token merging in BOTH vision encoder and LLM visual prefix: image-key diversity controls early merging, prompt-text relevance controls projected-token merging.
Training methodology: No training/fine-tuning/calibration; inference-time application to official pretrained models and jointly trained SigLIP text encoder.
Compression mechanism: AVTM score one minus mean cosine similarity of attention-key token to all others, retain if ≥ρ and merge others into most similar; ALVTM visual–pooled-text cosine, retain ≥τ and merge remaining into nearest retained token.
Relevance to our proposal: Closest direct collision: already handles question-guided variable visual count in a pretrained VLM, both vision/connector-side and decoder-side, without modifying decoder.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Novelty cannot be claimed solely for prompt-guided adaptive merging/variable count or frozen decoder; defensible gap is training vision+connector under frozen decoder with learned compute-aware policy/reward and looped-decoder-specific behavior, experimentally shown against AdaptMerge.
Method evidence (PDF pages): Sections 3.1–3.2.2 PDF pp.3–5, Figure 2 PDF p.4 and Eqs.1–3 PDF pp.4–5; thresholds in Sec.4.1 PDF p.6.
Experimental evidence (PDF pages): Sections 4.1–4.3 PDF pp.5–8, Tables 1–7 PDF pp.6–8; Limitations PDF p.9.
Question conditioning: Yes, ALVTM cosine-scores visual tokens against pooled text encoder embedding of actual prompt/question; AVTM is image-only diversity.
Adaptive budget: Yes: fixed diversity threshold ρ=0.05 and relevance threshold τ=0.15 yield image/prompt-dependent keep sets and variable token counts; no explicitly trained budget predictor or reward optimization.
Frozen components: Vision encoder, projector, text tower and LLM checkpoints remain unchanged; no learned connector/policy.
Training objective: Hand-set thresholds ρ,τ; no training objective, compute penalty, PPO/GRPO or reward; evaluated performance/TFLOPs post hoc.
Benchmarks: OKVQA; AI2D; ScienceQA-IMG; TextVQA; Gemma-3-4B/12B; LLaVA-1.5-7B
Reported results: Gemma-3-4B AI2D: 68.10 original vs 65.12 AdaptMerge; 7.91→5.12 TFLOPs; TextVQA 65.50→61.44 (Table 1, PDF p.6).; Gemma-3-4B AI2D L40: latency 0.711→0.399 s, throughput 1.41→2.51 samples/s, vision time 0.532→0.203 s (Table 2, PDF p.7); runtime comparison averages AI2D images without few-shot examples/pan-and-scan.; Gemma-3-12B AI2D 77.82→71.53, 12.87→8.87 TFLOPs; SQA 76.45→76.60 (Table 1, PDF p.6).; LLaVA-1.5-7B AI2D 53.50→51.30, 9.95→7.56 TFLOPs (Table 7, PDF p.8).; AVTM alone 6.08 TFLOPs/65.42 AI2D; ALVTM alone 7.17/65.38; combined 5.12/65.12 (Table 3, PDF p.7).
Limitations: Authors note dependence on guidance quality/noisy or ambiguous modalities and harder interpretability (Limitations, PDF p.9); heuristic thresholds not trained for optimal quality–compute tradeoff; baseline 4B AI2D loses ~3 points and TextVQA ~4 points despite lower compute.

Paper title: Chameleon: Mixed-Modal Early-Fusion Foundation Models
Primary contribution: Early-fusion autoregressive model generates/interprets mixed text and quantized image tokens in arbitrary sequences; contrasts connector-based frozen decoder assumptions.
Training methodology: Pretraining text/image/interleaved sequences with autoregressive next-token objective, followed by SFT mixture including visual chat; image tokenizer trained on licensed images.
Compression mechanism: Learned image VQ tokenizer; early fusion single AR sequence, QK norm/dropout/z-loss stabilization; supervised alignment on visual-chat/image-generation/mixed-modal tasks.
Relevance to our proposal: Generative visual-token baseline and illustration of fixed image code cost; mostly architecture background.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Not direct answer to pretrained looped VLM connector-only tuning; quantized tokens should not be confused with feature-token pruning.
Method evidence (PDF pages): Sections 2–2.4 PDF pp.4–8 (tokenization, architecture/stability), Section 3 PDF pp.9–10 (SFT).
Experimental evidence (PDF pages): Sections 4–5 PDF pp.11–17, especially Table 7 PDF p.17.
Question conditioning: Questions drive autoregressive answer generation, not choice of how many image tokens to encode.
Adaptive budget: Fixed 1024 image codes per 512×512 image; no learned per-question budget.
Frozen components: Decoder is fully trained/pretrained as foundation model then SFT; not frozen while training a vision connector.
Training objective: Autoregressive next-token likelihood plus stabilization z-loss; SFT alignment; no compute-budget/RL visual-token objective in described method.
Benchmarks: COCO captions; Flickr30k captions; VQAv2; text benchmarks; human preference evaluation; safety prompts
Reported results: 512×512 image encodes to 1024 discrete tokens, codebook 8192 (Section 2.1, PDF p.4).; Chameleon-34B pretrained: COCO CIDEr 120.2 (2-shot), Flickr30k 74.7 (2-shot), VQAv2 66.0 (2-shot); multi-task 34B VQAv2 69.6 (Table 7, PDF p.17).; Chameleon-SFT 34B COCO CIDEr 140.8 (0-shot) in Table 7 PDF p.17.
Limitations: Tokenizer explicitly struggles reconstructing text-rich images (Sec.2.1 p.4); enormous pretraining compute; architecture not a plug-in frozen decoder.
Warnings: Paper document is arXiv:2405.09818v2 dated March 21, 2025, although initial arXiv paper and core work originated 2024; year field uses original paper year; revised-version date noted.

Paper title: Emerging Properties in Self-Supervised Vision Transformers
Primary contribution: DINO self-distillation without labels yields semantically organized ViT features and unsupervised object boundaries; candidate frozen vision teacher/backbone, no VLM compression.
Training methodology: ImageNet unlabeled self-supervised pretraining with AdamW; student updated by gradients, teacher by EMA; downstream frozen k-NN/linear and optional finetuning.
Compression mechanism: EMA teacher, centered/sharpened distribution, cross-view cross entropy; multicrop augmentation; semantic CLS attention maps emerge.
Relevance to our proposal: Potential frozen visual foundation/teacher; dense structure informs whether compression discards needed regions.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Image saliency alone does not resolve task-dependent answer quality; use as backbone/control.
Method evidence (PDF pages): Section 3 PDF pp.2–5 (Figure 2, Algorithm 1 PDF p.3, student/teacher and centering).
Experimental evidence (PDF pages): Sections 4–5 PDF pp.5–9, Tables 1,2,5 PDF pp.4,5,7.
Question conditioning: None: no natural-language/question input to vision encoder.
Adaptive budget: No adaptive budget; 224² ViT-S/16 sequence 197 incl CLS and ViT-S/8 785 incl CLS (Table 1 PDF p.4).
Frozen components: EMA teacher no backprop; student vision model trainable during pretraining; no language decoder.
Training objective: Cross entropy between teacher probability on one view and student prediction on other, with teacher centering/sharpening; no image-text answer reward or compute loss.
Benchmarks: ImageNet k-NN/linear probe; ROxford/RParis image retrieval; Copydays; DAVIS-2017 segmentation
Reported results: DINO ViT-S ImageNet k-NN 74.5%, linear 77.0%; ViT-S/8 k-NN 78.3%, linear 79.7% (Table 2, PDF p.5).; DAVIS 2017 downstream segmentation uses frozen patch features and nearest neighbors, no task finetune (Section 4.2.3, PDF p.7).
Limitations: No multimodal/text supervision, so object saliency is not per-question relevance; finer patches drastically raise token count/compute.

Paper title: Harnessing Frozen Unimodal Encoders for Flexible Multimodal Alignment
Research category: Multimodal alignment and connector design; Vision encoder post-training
Primary contribution: Freeze-Align selects compatible pretrained unimodal image/text towers via CKA, curates concept-rich image-caption pairs, trains lightweight patch/CLS and text projectors only.
Training methodology: Precompute frozen encoder features and train projection layers on 20M image-caption mixture; CKA toy and real encoder-pair selection; no decoder finetuning.
Compression mechanism: CKA estimates encoder compatibility; 3000 concept prototypes retrieve 6M LAION samples; combine CC3M/CC12M/SBU into 20M MIX-CLASS-Collected; residual patch/CLS/text MLP projectors trained contrastively.
Relevance to our proposal: Closest parameter-freezing/connector training analogue among this batch, but optimizes global alignment rather than question-aware compression with frozen decoder.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Novelty must not claim frozen unimodal encoders plus connector-only training generally; target distinguishes frozen autoregressive decoder and learned visual budget.
Method evidence (PDF pages): Sections 3–4.3 PDF pp.3–5 (CKA, curation, 11M residual projectors, frozen encoders); Sec.5.2 PDF pp.5–6.
Experimental evidence (PDF pages): Sections 5–6 PDF pp.5–8, especially Tables 1–4 PDF pp.6–7.
Question conditioning: Text-image shared space learned, but no runtime visual patch selection conditioned on question.
Adaptive budget: No variable token budget or compute-aware routing.
Frozen components: Both unimodal encoders frozen, only projectors trained; not a frozen generative decoder architecture.
Training objective: CLIP-style image-text contrastive loss on projected features; no variable-length or latency reward.
Benchmarks: ImageNet/Imagenet-v2 zero-shot; Caltech; Pets; Cars; Flowers; Food; Aircrafts; SUN; CUB; UCF101; Flickr30k/COCO retrieval; multilingual tests; segmentation
Reported results: DINOv2-ARL with 20M alignment samples: ImageNet zero-shot 76.3%, ImageNet-v2 69.2% (Table 3, PDF p.7).; Flickr30k image-to-text R@1 87.5% and text-to-image 74.1%; COCO image-to-text 60.1%, text-to-image 45.1% (Table 4, PDF p.6).; Alignment data ablation: 6M LAION-CLASS-Collected ImageNet 76.12% versus 20M longer training 76.30%; latter Flickr I2T/T2I 87.54/74.17 (Table 2, PDF p.6).
Limitations: Compatibility depends on encoder-pair geometry and diverse/aligned dataset; no generative LLM decoding or compressed adaptive visual sequence.

Paper title: Gramian Multimodal Representation Learning and Alignment
Primary contribution: GRAM uses the Gram determinant/parallelotope volume for simultaneous alignment of two or more modality-level embeddings.
Training methodology: End-to-end pretraining of multimodal encoders with paired video/audio/text and retrieval fine-tuning; no looped VLM.
Compression mechanism: Normalize per-modality vectors; compute sqrt(det(A^T A)) for their joint volume; contrast positives versus negatives; optional data-anchor matching.
Relevance to our proposal: Low: possible auxiliary alignment regularizer only.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: No question-conditioned visual token selection, token-count decision or frozen looped decoder.
Question conditioning: None; text can be retrieval anchor but not a VQA-conditioned selector.
Adaptive budget: None.
Frozen components: No frozen language decoder is specified as a design constraint.
Training objective: Symmetric volume-based contrastive loss (data-to-anchor/anchor-to-data) plus 0.1× binary data-anchor matching.
Benchmarks: MSR-VTT; DiDeMo; ActivityNet; VATEX; AudioCaps; VGGSound 5K
Reported results: Zero-shot MSR-VTT text-to-video R@1: 54.2 for text-video-audio GRAM versus 49.3 VAST (Table 1); fine-tuned text-video-audio: 58.4 versus 55.8 (Table 2). AudioCaps zero-shot text-to-audio via text-audiovisual R@1 33.2 versus 32.1 VAST (Table 3).
Limitations: Alignment of whole-modality vectors is distinct from localized token retention; minimizing volume alone can also favor linearly dependent antiparallel vectors (geometric caveat); no adaptive compute evaluation.
Warnings: Gram-volume alignment is not equivalent to cosine closeness for opposite vectors; do not confuse with GRAM-based image patch pruning.

Paper title: ImageBind: One Embedding Space To Bind Them All
Primary contribution: Aligns image, text, audio, depth, thermal and IMU in a shared embedding using image-paired modality data; unobserved modality pairs align emergently.
Training methodology: Image and text encoders frozen; audio/depth/thermal/IMU encoders updated against paired image data.
Compression mechanism: Symmetric image–other-modality InfoNCE, with images as the bridge to shared embedding space.
Relevance to our proposal: Low: pretraining encoder analogy for frozen modules.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Strong encoder alignment but no connector-to-frozen-decoder VQA or variable visual-token count.
Question conditioning: None; text prompts used for zero-shot classification/retrieval, not image-token selection.
Adaptive budget: None.
Frozen components: Image and text encoders; no autoregressive language decoder.
Training objective: Symmetric InfoNCE contrastive alignment.
Benchmarks: AudioSet; ESC; VGGSound; NYU Depth; SUN Depth; MSR-VTT; Clotho; AudioCaps; Ego4D
Reported results: Emergent zero-shot ESC audio classification top-1 66.9%; MSR-VTT text-to-video retrieval R@1 36.8 with audio+video (Table 4); Clotho text-to-audio R@1 6.0 (Table 3).
Limitations: Image-centric shared embedding does not learn question-specific dense spatial tokens or downstream answer fidelity; no adaptive visual budget.
Warnings: Do not interpret image-text emergent retrieval as visual-token compression.

Paper title: Matryoshka Multimodal Models
Research category: Adaptive visual token compression; Multimodal alignment and connector design; Vision encoder post-training; Supervised and differentiable compression; Knowledge distillation; Adaptive computation and reasoning depth
Primary contribution: Trains a single VLM to function at nested visual token scales; demonstrates an oracle gap and explicitly proposes an image/question-based scale predictor as future work.
Training methodology: Fine-tunes visual encoder and entire LLM from pretrained LLaVA weights for one epoch; average next-token answer NLL across all five visual scales per example.
Compression mechanism: Hierarchical 2×2/3×3 average pooling; same weights support all scales and no added learned controller in the implemented model.
Relevance to our proposal: Very high: direct multi-budget training and explicit unfilled routing gap.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Closest baseline for nested budgets; proposed target can add question-conditioned learned count, frozen decoder, and compute-aware/RL learning.
Experimental evidence (PDF pages): §4.2–4.5, PDF pp.6–9, especially Tables 1–2 pp.6 and oracle discussion/limitations pp.8–9.
Question conditioning: Question conditions answer loss, not the granularity choice; explicit image- or question-conditioned predictor is unimplemented future work (§4.4).
Adaptive budget: Manually select one of five scales at inference; oracle chooses cheapest correctly answered scale using ground truth and is not realizable as a deployed policy.
Frozen components: Decoder is NOT frozen; ablation finds training whole LLM better than training CLIP alone (Table 7, PDF p.9).
Training objective: Mean autoregressive answer NLL across all token scales; no explicit compute penalty or RL.
Benchmarks: MMBench; GQA; POPE; VizWiz; SEEDBench; TextVQA; AI2D; ChartQA; DocVQA; ScienceQA; MMMU; MSVD-QA; MSRVTT-QA; ActivityNet-QA; NExT-QA; IntentQA; EgoSchema
Reported results: LLaVA-1.5-M3 MMBench: 65.9 at 576 tokens, 63.1 at 9, 59.5 at 1 (Table 1, PDF p.6). LLaVA-NeXT-M3 MMBench: 69.50 at 144/grid and 67.35 at 9/grid versus 67.96 at 576/grid (Table 2). TextVQA drops from 63.13 at 576/grid to 51.97 at 9/grid. Oracle TextVQA row: 31.39 average tokens/grid at 70.51, not a real learned policy (Table 2).
Limitations: No automatic per-question scale predictor; full LLM training conflicts with frozen-decoder constraint; coarse average pooling loses text/OCR detail; evaluating all scales during training adds compute.
Warnings: Oracle uses correctness at all scales and ground truth, so its numbers are not measured automatic adaptive routing; LLaVA-NeXT table #tokens is per image grid, not always overall image tokens.

Paper title: NExT-GPT: Any-to-Any Multimodal LLM
Primary contribution: Lightweight adapters connect ImageBind inputs and frozen diffusion outputs through Vicuna for any-to-any text/image/audio/video tasks.
Training methodology: Input adapter X-to-caption alignment with frozen LLM; output-side caption/denoising alignment and multimodal instruction tuning; Vicuna LoRA is updated, alongside input/output projections.
Compression mechanism: Learned concept grouping of modality patch tokens; separate modality-specific generation signal tokens.
Relevance to our proposal: Moderate: grouped connector with mostly frozen backbone.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Architecture trains small adapter but does not learn input image token budget or freeze Vicuna LoRA.
Method evidence (PDF pages): §3–4, PDF pp.3–6; Table 1 p.4 and Fig.2 p.5.
Question conditioning: Questions may drive response, but input concept-token count is not an adaptive policy.
Adaptive budget: No per-example visual-token count; fixed architecture and modality-specific output signal-token hyperparameters.
Frozen components: ImageBind and diffusion decoders frozen; Vicuna base frozen but LoRA trained (Table 1); not strictly frozen decoder including adapters.
Training objective: Caption next-token cross entropy, output caption alignment and diffusion denoising/contrastive alignment, then supervised multimodal instruction tuning.
Benchmarks: NoCaps; Flickr30K; COCO; VQAv2; VizWiz; OKVQA; MMBench; SEED; MSVD-QA; MSRVTT-QA; NExTQA; AudioCaps
Reported results: PDF Table 2 (p.7) reports NExT-GPT VQAv2 66.7 and MMBench 58.0; Table 4 reports text-to-image FID 10.07 and text-to-audio FAD 1.68. Grouping is compared to linear/Q-Former alternatives (§6.2, p.8).
Limitations: Generation-oriented adapters and separate diffusion backends; no dynamic count or token-cost tradeoff; output signal token ablation does not test input token compression.
Warnings: Table 1 explicitly lists 33M Vicuna LoRA parameters trainable; avoid describing the entire LLM as frozen.

Paper title: Unified-IO 2: Scaling Autoregressive Multimodal Models with Vision, Language, Audio, and Action
Primary contribution: Unified encoder-decoder trained from scratch for diverse multimodal input/output tasks; fixed resampling of image/audio histories reduces context cost.
Training methodology: Trains shared encoder-decoder from scratch; pretrained ViT and AST frozen during pretraining, fine-tuned at end of instruction tuning.
Compression mechanism: Perceiver latent query resampling for history; 2D RoPE, QK normalization, scaled cosine attention stabilize heterogeneous training.
Relevance to our proposal: Moderate: demonstrates fixed Perceiver bottleneck and image-history compression.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: No per-query budget selection, frozen decoder, or compute-aware learning; dynamic packing is unrelated.
Question conditioning: Task prompt conditions transformer generation, but Perceiver resampling count does not depend on question.
Adaptive budget: No adaptive visual count; dynamic packing/unpacking is training throughput batching, not example-wise visual budget.
Frozen components: Vision/audio encoders temporarily frozen; autoregressive decoder trained from scratch, not frozen.
Training objective: Mixture of denoising tasks with autoregressive text/image/audio prediction and dynamic masking; no token-cost RL.
Benchmarks: GRIT; VQAv2; OKVQA; ScienceQA; RefCOCO; COCO caption; POPE; SEED; MMBench; AudioCaps; Objectron
Reported results: UIO-2XXL (6.8B) VQAv2 79.4, MMBench 71.5, POPE 87.7 (Table 5, PDF p.10); GRIT overall 2.7 points above prior Unified-IO reported §5.2 p.9.
Limitations: Large train-from-scratch model, fixed resampling, image/audio generation quality and niche modality limitations (§6 p.11).
Warnings: The 32-token image history resampling is fixed; do not mistake dynamic packing for adaptive vision tokenization. Paper PDF is Dec 2023 version, notwithstanding subsequent publication.

Paper title: VALOR: Vision-Audio-Language Omni-Perception Pretraining Model and Dataset
Primary contribution: Joint visual/audio/language pretraining via groupwise contrastive alignment and captioning with VALOR-1M/VALOR-32K.
Training methodology: End-to-end encoder/decoder pretraining on VALOR-1M plus image/video-caption data; downstream adaptation to retrieval, captioning and QA.
Compression mechanism: Multimodal grouping alignment (MGA) and captioning (MGC) over text-video, text-audio, text-audiovisual subsets.
Relevance to our proposal: Low: possible multimodal conditioning/control baseline.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Modality grouping is not adaptive token compression; decoder is not frozen.
Question conditioning: QA downstream via decoder, but no question-aware token pruning or count choice.
Adaptive budget: None; training modality group choice (T-V/T-A/T-AV) is not an input-conditional token budget.
Frozen components: Not a frozen pretrained language decoder scheme; cross-attention and unimodal encoders trained.
Training objective: Weighted groupwise contrastive MGA plus autoregressive/causal masked-token MGC; some reported VATEX generation comparisons involve task-specific RL, not token-budget policy.
Benchmarks: VALOR-32K; MSRVTT; DiDeMo; ActivityNet; VATEX; MSRVTT-QA; MSVD-QA; TGIF-FrameQA; MUSIC-AVQA; AudioCaps; ClothoV1; VQAv2
Reported results: VALOR-B text-to-audiovisual VALOR-32K retrieval R@1 67.9 with V+A versus 43.3 visual-only (Table 3, PDF p.9); VALOR-L MSRVTT-QA 49.2 and MUSIC-AVQA 78.9 (Table 5, PDF p.10).
Limitations: End-to-end multimodal pretraining and modality-specific benchmarks; no measured vision-token count/FLOP frontier.
Warnings: The RL note in VATEX captioning Table 4 is a generation metric training trick, not visual-token cost RL; PDF revision dated Jan 2025.

Paper title: Flamingo: a Visual Language Model for Few-Shot Learning
Primary contribution: Interleaves trainable gated vision cross-attention layers into a frozen LM and maps variable vision-encoder grids to a fixed 64 visual tokens per image/video.
Training methodology: Train resampler, gated cross-attention and newly inserted dense blocks with mixture of interleaved M3W, image-text pairs, video-text pairs; frozen vision backbone and pretrained LM blocks.
Compression mechanism: Learned latent queries cross-attend variable-size image/video feature grid; per-image cross-attention masking prevents direct access to previous images.
Relevance to our proposal: High: canonical frozen-LM/learned visual compression architecture.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Direct baseline for fixed learned resampling but no dynamic question-conditioned count or cost objective.
Question conditioning: Text attends to visual tokens downstream; Perceiver resampling is image-only, not conditioned on the specific question.
Adaptive budget: Fixed 64 tokens per visual input; number of image/video inputs may vary but token count per input does not.
Frozen components: Pretrained NFNet visual encoder and LM layers; new gated cross-attention and dense layers trainable.
Training objective: Weighted mixture of per-dataset conditional autoregressive text NLL; no token-cost loss/RL.
Benchmarks: VQAv2; COCO caption; VATEX; VizWiz; MSRVTT-QA; OKVQA; TextVQA; HatefulMemes; VisDial; MSVD-QA
Reported results: Flamingo-80B 32-shot VQAv2 test-dev 67.6 and COCO CIDEr 113.8; fine-tuned VQAv2 test-dev 82.0 (Table 2, PDF p.8). Flamingo-3B Perceiver baseline ablation COCO CIDEr 86.5 vs 78.6 when replaced by MLP (Table 3, p.8).
Limitations: 64-token bottleneck cannot adapt detail per question; proprietary training data/models in original report; inserted trainable LM-adjacent cross-attention layers.
Warnings: Frozen LM blocks do not mean no trainable components in LM stack: gated cross-attention/dense blocks are newly inserted and trained.

Paper title: BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models
Primary contribution: Two-stage Q-Former alignment bridges frozen image encoder and frozen LLM using 32 learned queries.
Training methodology: Stage 1 representation training with image-text contrastive (ITC), image-text matching (ITM), image-grounded text generation (ITG); stage 2 train Q-Former+FC using frozen LLM language modeling.
Compression mechanism: Trainable cross-attention queries gather information from frozen encoder; projected queries prepended to LLM text embeddings.
Relevance to our proposal: High: direct frozen-decoder fixed-bottleneck baseline.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Dynamic question-conditioned count and looped decoder with compute objective would extend rather than reproduce BLIP-2.
Question conditioning: Stage-1 queries learn text-relevant image features over dataset; inference queries are NOT conditioned by current question; text prompt appended to LLM after visual projection.
Adaptive budget: Fixed 32 learned visual queries independent of question/image complexity.
Frozen components: Image encoder and LLM in pretraining; image encoder fine-tuned for COCO retrieval in a separate downstream evaluation (§4.4).
Training objective: ITC+ITM+ITG, then next-token/prefix LM NLL; no explicit token-cost loss/RL.
Benchmarks: VQAv2; OK-VQA; GQA; NoCaps; COCO Caption; Flickr30K retrieval
Reported results: ViT-g/FlanT5XXL zero-shot VQAv2 test-dev 65.0 with 108M trainable parameters (Table 2, PDF p.6); zero-shot NoCaps CIDEr 121.6 for ViT-g/FlanT5XL (Table 3, p.7).
Limitations: Fixed query count, question-agnostic extraction; no improved VQA in-context learning in reported tests (§5 p.8); retrieval fine-tuning changes encoder freezing.
Warnings: 188M Q-Former is total module size, while 103–108M trainable in reported stage-2 zero-shot VQA variants (Table 2); avoid mixing stages.

Paper title: InstructBLIP: Towards General-purpose Vision-Language Models with Instruction Tuning
Research category: Question-conditioned vision encoding; Multimodal alignment and connector design; Vision encoder post-training; Supervised and differentiable compression
Primary contribution: Feeds instruction text into BLIP-2 Q-Former so 32 learned visual queries become task-conditioned while vision encoder and LLM stay frozen.
Training methodology: Finetunes Q-Former from BLIP-2 checkpoints with language modeling response loss on 13 held-in datasets; keeps ViT-g and LLM frozen.
Compression mechanism: Instruction-conditioned query-image cross-attention via query/text self-attention; dataset-size sqrt reweighting for multi-task instruction tuning.
Relevance to our proposal: Very high: already implements question-conditioned frozen-decoder visual connector.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Closest overlap: cannot claim question-conditioned connector as novel; adaptive count, looped decoder integration and compute-aware/RL objective must be clearly differentiated.
Question conditioning: Yes: actual instruction tokens enter Q-Former self-attention alongside learnable queries and affect extracted image features.
Adaptive budget: No: query count K fixed (BLIP-2 initialization uses 32); response length adaptation does not entail vision-token count adaptation.
Frozen components: Image encoder and LLM frozen during instruction tuning; trainable Q-Former (and any projection handling should not be overstated).
Training objective: Supervised response next-token NLL; no visual-token-cost reward or RL.
Benchmarks: GQA; TextVQA; ScienceQA; IconQA; VizWiz; iVQA; MSVD-QA; MSRVTT-QA; NoCaps; Flickr30K; HatefulMemes; Visual Dialog
Reported results: FlanT5XL GQA 48.4 vs 45.9 without instruction-aware visual features; ScienceQA image-context 70.4 vs 63.4; VizWiz 32.7 vs 25.1 (Table 2, PDF p.7). InstructBLIP Vicuna-7B iVQA 52.2 vs 36.8 without instruction-awareness (Table 2).
Limitations: Fixed visual token count, fixed pretrained frozen vision features; no compute-aware controller; OCR tokens inserted into some instructions (§2.2), a confound for pure-image comparisons.
Warnings: Do not label the question-aware extractor novel; distinguish query content adaptivity from count adaptivity. Video evaluation uses four frames with separately run Q-Former (§2.5 p.6).

Paper title: Visual Instruction Tuning
Research category: Multimodal alignment and connector design; Foundational and background literature
Primary contribution: GPT-4-synthesized language-image instructions train a CLIP-to-Vicuna VLM with lightweight linear visual projection.
Training methodology: Stage 1 CC3M-595K caption alignment trains only W with frozen vision+LM; stage 2 trains W and Vicuna LM on 158K generated instruction samples; ScienceQA separately fine-tuned.
Compression mechanism: Linear alignment of vision embeddings to LM embedding space; two-stage caption alignment then visual instruction fine-tuning.
Relevance to our proposal: Moderate: architecture and stage-1 frozen-LM connector baseline.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Strong source model for adaptation, but target requires compression, dynamic count and fully frozen looped decoder.
Method evidence (PDF pages): §4.1–4.2, PDF pp.4–5; Eq.1 p.4, training stages p.5.
Question conditioning: Question text in LLM input, not vision connector/projection.
Adaptive budget: None; fixed visual grid output.
Frozen components: CLIP vision encoder frozen throughout; Vicuna LM frozen only stage 1, trainable stage 2.
Training objective: Assistant answer autoregressive next-token NLL, masking non-answer parts; no compute penalty or RL.
Benchmarks: LLaVA-Bench; ScienceQA
Reported results: ScienceQA LLaVA accuracy 90.92%; LLaVA + text-only GPT-4 judge 92.53% (Table 7, PDF pp.8–9); skipping alignment pretraining 85.81% (Table 8 p.9).
Limitations: No actual visual token reduction or adaptive cost; decoder not frozen during final instruction tuning; GPT-4 judge ensemble is external, not LLaVA-alone.
Warnings: 92.53% is a judge ensemble using text-only GPT-4; standalone LLaVA is 90.92%. Frozen decoder claim only valid for stage 1.

Paper title: Cambrian-1: A Fully Open, Vision-Centric Exploration of Multimodal LLMs
Research category: Multimodal alignment and connector design; Vision encoder post-training; Supervised and differentiable compression
Primary contribution: Spatial Vision Aggregator (SVA) integrates four visual towers at disparate resolutions through spatially aligned latent grids and repeated visual cross-attention within LLM; introduces CV-Bench.
Training methodology: Connector alignment followed by multimodal instruction tuning on Cambrian data; examines frozen/unfrozen vision settings.
Compression mechanism: Spatially restricted local cross-attention, D layers and G groups; 576-to-36 single-encoder ablation.
Relevance to our proposal: Strong connector baseline and vision-centric evaluation.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Can replace SVA static grid with question-conditioned variable-size queries while holding LLM fixed; repeated cross-attention would violate strict frozen-decoder architectural constraint.
Method evidence (PDF pages): §4 Spatial Vision Aggregator PDF pp.13–15; §3.3 instruction recipe p.8.
Experimental evidence (PDF pages): §4 Table 4 p.15; Table 5 p.16; §3.2 CV-Bench pp.7–8; Table 9 p.20.
Question conditioning: No: learnable grid queries do not ingest user question.
Adaptive budget: No sample-adaptive token count; latent grid size/groups configured statically.
Frozen components: Stage dependent; visual backbone frozen in initial alignment, alternatives unfreeze during instruction tuning; LLM not universally frozen.
Training objective: Multimodal answer/instruction learning, not reward-minus-compute.
Benchmarks: CV-Bench; MMMU; TextVQA; ChartQA; DocVQA; MMVP; MME; AI2D
Reported results: CV-Bench has 2,638 curated examples. SVA versus resampler OCR/chart category 55.5 versus 27.1; SVA versus interpolation+MLP in single encoder compression 31.4 versus 28.1 OCR/chart. Cambrian-1-8B uses 576 visual tokens and scores 73.1 on MMBench and 49.0 on MathVista (Table 9).
Limitations: Multi-tower compute and added LLM cross-attention; no question-specific selection or explicit per-example compute reward.
Warnings: PDF p.9 text extraction corrupt; table figures verified on pp.15–16 and 20.

Paper title: MM1: Methods, Analysis & Insights from Multimodal LLM Pre-training
Research category: Multimodal alignment and connector design; Foundational and background literature
Primary contribution: Controlled connector, resolution, encoder and data-mixture ablations; final 144-token connector.
Training methodology: Initializes vision encoder and LLM from pretrained checkpoints, then trains entire MM1 unfrozen for 200k steps (~400B tokens) with 45% interleaved, 45% captions, 10% text-only. SFT on ~1.45M examples.
Compression mechanism: Compares average pooling, attention pooling, C-Abstractor; resolution/token count more important than connector type in studies.
Relevance to our proposal: Static-token reference and data-control baseline.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Shows token count and resolution affect performance; motivates comparing question-conditioned compression at matched connector capacity.
Method evidence (PDF pages): §3.2 pp.6–8; §4 Final Model and Training Recipe p.10.
Question conditioning: No; connector is image-only.
Adaptive budget: No; final 144 fixed visual tokens.
Frozen components: None in final multimodal pretraining; all models entirely unfrozen.
Training objective: Autoregressive pretraining and supervised finetuning; no compute-aware token policy.
Benchmarks: VQAv2; TextVQA; VizWiz; OKVQA; COCO; NoCaps; MMMU; MME
Reported results: Final MM1-30B 8-shot VQAv2 70.9 and TextVQA 49.4 (pretraining Table 3); synthetic VeCap improves few-shot performance 2.4 and 4 absolute points in ablations.
Limitations: Ablations are mainly pretraining/large model design; no decoder freezing or per-question token optimization.

Paper title: PaliGemma: A versatile 3B VLM for transfer
Research category: Multimodal alignment and connector design; Foundational and background literature
Primary contribution: Transfer-oriented SigLIP/Gemma VLM with resolution-specific checkpoints; causal-mask and tuning ablations.
Training methodology: Stage1 full-model pretraining on 1B examples at 224px; Stage2 high-resolution continuations; downstream transfer fine-tunes all weights.
Compression mechanism: Prefix-LM mask: image and question prefix bidirectional, answer suffix autoregressive; loss on answer suffix.
Relevance to our proposal: Benchmark for frozen-decoder counterfactual and resolution-token scaling.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Strong control for whether freezing pretrained decoder is adequate, though authors optimize broad transfer rather than compute-aware policy.
Question conditioning: Text prompts condition generated output but not image token count.
Adaptive budget: Three fixed resolution checkpoints, selected by task rather than per-instance question policy.
Frozen components: No component permanently frozen in main Stage1/transfer; freezing ViT/LLM studied in ablations.
Training objective: Next-token prediction over answer suffix; no compute penalty.
Benchmarks: 38 transfer tasks; COCO; DocVQA; ChartQA; RefCOCO
Reported results: At Stage1 224px 256 image tokens; at 448px four 224 patches worth / 1024 tokens; at 896px 4096 tokens. Figure 7 shows freezing language component significantly worsens transfer, whereas frozen ViT is near all-tuned after transfers, despite spatial-task validation perplexity worsening.
Limitations: No learned dynamic budget, task transfers usually all weights; high-res token costs substantial.

Paper title: Pixtral 12B
Research category: Multimodal alignment and connector design; Foundational and background literature
Primary contribution: Native-aspect-ratio variable-resolution vision encoder and fair benchmark prompt evaluation.
Training methodology: Vision encoder trained from scratch; multimodal training strategy not fully specified in inspected main methods.
Compression mechanism: Image break/end markers encode rows; 2D rotary visual positions support different resolutions; fully connected projector.
Relevance to our proposal: Dynamic-resolution comparison baseline; benchmark protocol caution.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Separates native-size variable tokens from question-conditioned adaptive count; prompt formatting can confound apparent rewards.
Method evidence (PDF pages): §2 Architectural details pp.3–4; §3 benchmark design p.5.
Experimental evidence (PDF pages): §4 Table 2 p.6; prompt/flexible parsing Tables 4–5 pp.7–8.
Question conditioning: No; question affects answer only.
Adaptive budget: Variable tokens with native image dimensions, not learned question-conditioned budgeting.
Frozen components: Not documented as decoder-frozen; do not assume it.
Training objective: Multimodal generative training, not cost-aware reward.
Benchmarks: MM-MT-Bench; MMMU; MathVista; ChartQA; DocVQA; VQAv2
Reported results: Under paper evaluation Pixtral 12B scores MMMU 52.0, MathVista 58.3, ChartQA 81.8, DocVQA 90.7, MM-MT-Bench 6.05. 92-conversation MM-MT-Bench correlates 0.91 with LMSys Vision Elo.
Limitations: Resolution-driven count may be large; no learned compute-quality budget and prompt/metric dependence substantial.

Paper title: DeepSeek-OCR: Contexts Optical Compression
Primary contribution: Optical compression of document text via high-resolution DeepEncoder with 16× compression and selectable multi-resolution token modes.
Training methodology: Encoder pretraining with compact LM next-token objective; final pipeline freezes SAM and compressor, trains CLIP and MoE decoder on OCR/general vision data.
Compression mechanism: 16× downsampling of spatial tokens; tiled local views plus global view for large documents.
Relevance to our proposal: High-compression backbone and quality-vs-token curve.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Distinct from answer-focused question-conditioned variable token count; useful stress test for tiny visual budgets and OCR-heavy questions.
Question conditioning: No; prompt selects OCR output style but resolution/token count not conditioned on question semantics.
Adaptive budget: Discrete native modes 64/100/256/400 tokens and dynamic tiling n×100+256 or n×256+400; mode/resolution chosen externally.
Frozen components: SAM and compressor frozen during final stage; decoder not frozen.
Training objective: OCR autoregressive reconstruction; measured compression ratios, no compute-penalized policy reward.
Benchmarks: Fox OCR compression; OmniDocBench
Reported results: On Fox English documents with 600–1300 text tokens, reported >96% decoding precision at ~9–10× text compression, ~90% at 10–12× and ~60% at 20× (§1 and Table 2). 100 visual tokens (640px mode) surpass GOT-OCR2.0 256 tokens on OmniDocBench per §4.2.
Limitations: Document OCR specialization; output accuracy falls sharply at extreme compression; visual preprocessing mode is not question-aware.

Paper title: EVEv2: Improved Baselines for Encoder-Free Vision-Language Models
Primary contribution: Decoder-native visual encoding with modality-aware attention/FFN/norm branches, avoiding standalone pretrained ViT.
Training methodology: Stage 1 patch embedding only (10M recap); Stage 2 vision layers with text/LLM layers frozen (29M→48M); subsequent joint alignment (15M) and SFT (7M) updates visual/text branches.
Compression mechanism: Divide-and-conquer modality routing within shared causal transformer; visual patch stem.
Relevance to our proposal: Frozen-language-stage comparison, architecture alternative.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Demonstrates modality-specific training can preserve original text weights early, but no connector-only dynamic visual token reduction.
Question conditioning: No question-conditioned token policy.
Adaptive budget: Input resolution variable but no per-question learned budget.
Frozen components: Text LLM layers frozen in stages 1/2; unfrozen in joint stages; final model not frozen-decoder adaptation.
Training objective: Next-token prediction plus visual instruction tuning; no compute reward.
Benchmarks: MMMU; MMBench-EN; SEEDBench-IMG; MMVet; TextVQA; ChartQA; AI2D; OCRBench
Reported results: EVEv2.0 7B Table 2: max 2500 visual tokens; MMMU 39.3; TextVQA 71.1; ChartQA 73.9; AI2D 74.8; OCRBench 702.
Limitations: Substantial visual sequence; native decoder alteration conflicts with strict frozen pretrained decoder; no adaptive budget.

Paper title: LLaVA-Mini: Efficient Image and Video Large Multimodal Models with One Vision Token
Research category: Adaptive visual token compression; Question-conditioned vision encoding; Multimodal alignment and connector design; Vision encoder post-training; Supervised and differentiable compression
Primary contribution: Question/text embeddings pre-fuse with full visual tokens before reducing to as few as one image token for LLM.
Training methodology: Appendix Table 9: Stage 1 alignment trains projector only, with vision encoder and LLM frozen; Stage 2 instruction tuning trains projector, compression module, pre-fusion module and LLM; vision encoder stays frozen. Batch 256, 1 and 2 epochs.
Compression mechanism: 2D-positioned learnable compression queries and pre-fusion preserve answer-specific information via text tokens.
Relevance to our proposal: Closest connector-level question-dependent information preservation baseline.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Need explicitly distinguish pre-fusing text with all image features from selecting a sample-dependent number of visual tokens; strong one-token baseline.
Method evidence (PDF pages): §4.1 pp.5–6; §4.2 p.6; Appendix B implementation p.18 and Table 9 p.19.
Experimental evidence (PDF pages): §5 Tables 1–3 pp.7–8; §5.3 Table 6/7 and Fig.7 p.9.
Question conditioning: Yes for text-token pre-fusion (instruction attends visual features); compressed vision queries themselves are learned static queries, not explicitly conditioned on question.
Adaptive budget: No per-example variable count; C² fixed by chosen configuration (one token standard; 64 high-res variant).
Frozen components: Vision encoder frozen in both stages; LLM frozen only in Stage 1, trainable in Stage 2. This is not frozen-decoder final adaptation.
Training objective: Supervised response learning, no explicit token-cost reward.
Benchmarks: VQAv2; GQA; TextVQA; MMBench; MVBench; MLVU; EgoSchema
Reported results: At 336px one visual token LLaVA-Mini Vicuna-7B gets VQAv2 77.6, GQA 60.9, MMBench 65.6 versus LLaVA-1.5 576 tokens: 78.5, 62.0, 64.3. MVBench average 44.5; model reports 0.6MB per video frame token storage versus LLaVA-1.5 358MB.
Limitations: Pre-fused question information in text tokens changes mechanism relative to purely vision-token question-conditioned router; fixed C, not learned compute-quality allocation.

Paper title: LLaVA-PruMerge: Adaptive Token Reduction for Efficient Large Multimodal Models
Research category: Adaptive visual token compression; Token pruning and merging
Primary contribution: Unsupervised image-complexity-adaptive visual token selection using ViT CLS attention outliers, then similarity clustering/merge.
Training methodology: Plug-and-play reduction; LLaVA-1.5 further finetuned with LoRA for one epoch on 665K instruction examples; video transfer tested training-free.
Compression mechanism: Penultimate-layer CLS-to-patch attention outlier detection, k-NN on key similarities and weighted cluster aggregation.
Relevance to our proposal: Direct adaptive-count prior art.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Novelty must be question-conditioned answer/cost policy and frozen decoder training, not adaptive token count alone.
Question conditioning: No user question conditioning; CLS-attention estimates image-intrinsic importance.
Adaptive budget: Yes: IQR outlier count naturally varies by image complexity; PruMerge+ supplements with prescribed sampling ratio.
Frozen components: Video-LLaVA inference-only variant freezes all weights; image results use LoRA, not wholly frozen decoder.
Training objective: No learned compute-penalized reward; attention/IQR heuristic.
Benchmarks: VQAv2; ScienceQA-IMG; TextVQA; POPE; MME; MMBench; MSVD-QA; MSRVTT-QA
Reported results: PruMerge and PruMerge+ average 5.5% and 25.0% original visual tokens across six tasks. Vicuna-7B PruMerge: VQAv2 72.0, MMBench 60.9 versus base 78.5/64.3; PruMerge+ 76.8/64.9. V100 FP16 Vicuna-7B prefill 88.6→15.3 ms with PruMerge (Table 2).
Limitations: CLS ignores question; no trainable cost-aware allocator; adaptation follows visual salience alone.
Warnings: Filename 2025 but arXiv id 2403.15388 (2024 first submission); inspected PDF is v6 dated Jan 31 2026. Year=2024 for originating paper, not v6 date.

Paper title: NVILA: Efficient Frontier Visual Language Models
Primary contribution: Scale high-resolution tiles and video frames then compress spatial and temporal token grids; studies data selection and training/deployment efficiency.
Training methodology: Adds visual encoder pretraining to recover compressed visual quality; multimodal pretraining/SFT, DeltaLoss data selection, FP8/fine-tuning strategies.
Compression mechanism: Dynamic-S2 tiling, spatial 3×3 pooling 256→121 tokens/tile, optional encoder pretraining, temporal pooling.
Relevance to our proposal: Strong scale-then-compress comparator and compute measurements.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Useful to compare per-question allocation against per-image tiling and generic temporal pooling at controlled spatial resolution.
Experimental evidence (PDF pages): Table 1 p.5; Tables 5–8 pp.7–8; Table 10 p.10; Fig.5 p.11.
Question conditioning: No question-conditioned visual routing; DeltaLoss ranks training examples, not inference token decisions.
Adaptive budget: Image tile counts vary with size/aspect ratio, but spatial pooling ratios and temporal averaging are configured globally rather than question-adaptive.
Frozen components: Fine-tuning recipe can use LoRA/QLoRA for LLM and ViT layer norms; main pipeline not a permanently frozen decoder.
Training objective: Supervised multimodal learning and DeltaLoss dataset selection, not reward per token.
Benchmarks: AI2D; DocVQA; TextVQA; MMMU; Video-MME; MLVU
Reported results: Spatial ablation: Dynamic-S2 scale baseline IM-10 71.5, 3×3 compressed 67.1, adding VEP 70.8; DocVQA 91.1→82.3→88.8. NVILA-8B with 256 frames: Video-MME with subtitles 70.0, MLVU 70.1 (Table 10).
Limitations: Fixed pooling ratios; no answer-dependent token policy; inference gains include quantization/engine changes besides token compression.
Warnings: Filename says 2025, manuscript is arXiv:2412.04468 (2024 first posted) but this PDF is v3 dated Apr 25/28 2026; year=2024 origin.

Paper title: DeepSeek-OCR 2: Visual Causal Flow
Research category: Question-conditioned vision encoding; Vision encoder post-training
Primary contribution: Replace CLIP in DeepEncoder with LLM-style bidirectional visual stream plus causal learnable flow queries to reorder visual information at 256–1120 tokens.
Training methodology: Three stages: train encoder with lightweight LM next-token supervision; freeze visual tokenizer while optimizing LM encoder+decoder for query enhancement; freeze whole encoder and train decoder continuation.
Compression mechanism: Dual attention mask: original image tokens bidirectional, flow-query suffix causal, queries attend all vision tokens and preceding queries.
Relevance to our proposal: Potential visual encoder design for richer token ordering under fixed small budgets.

Benchmarks: OmniDocBench v1.5
Reported results: OmniDocBench v1.5: OCR2 91.09 overall versus OCR1 87.36, max visual tokens 1120 versus 1156; overall edit distance 0.100 versus 0.129 in Table 2.
Limitations: OCR-centric; encoder+decoder jointly optimized in query stage; flow order not question-driven.

Primary contribution: Joint vision-text pretraining and visual RL; separate parallel-agent RL learns when to spawn frozen agents under critical-step resource measure.

Training objective: Outcome-based vision RL; critical-path/critical-step objective is for agent parallelism, not visual token cost.
Benchmarks: MMMU-Pro; MathVision; CharXiv; OCRBench; Video-MME; OSWorld
Reported results: Early fusion 10% vision ratio ablation vision OCR 65.7 vs mid 64.1 and late 61.5 (Table 1). Vision RL raises text MMLU-Pro 84.7→86.4, GPQA-Diamond 84.3→86.4 (Table 2).

Paper title: LLaVA-UHD v4: What Makes Efficient Visual Encoding in MLLMs?
Research category: Adaptive visual token compression; Token pruning and merging; Multimodal alignment and connector design; Vision encoder post-training
Primary contribution: Move a 4× compression block into shallow vision-transformer layers, preserving representations by preceding-layer parameter reuse and local attention.
Training methodology: Four stages: projector+D alignment; ViT-only knowledge injection; interleaved multimodal training; instruction SFT.
Compression mechanism: 2×2 local window attention, PixelUnshuffle to 4d channels, MLP fuse to d; initialize from preceding ViT attention/FFN weights.
Relevance to our proposal: Highly relevant placement and FLOPs-control comparator.

Benchmarks: MMMU; MathVista; MMBench EN/CN; MMStar; HallusionBench; AI2D; OCRBench
Reported results: Single-slice visual encoding FLOPs 3555.1G post-ViT baseline to 1573.1G with early compressor (reported −55.75%); across 4M–64M data scales average accuracy differs only −0.29 points on average. At 4M, baseline 70.6 versus 70.7 for ours.

Paper title: Molmo2: Open Weights and Data for Vision-Language Models with Video Understanding and Grounding
Primary contribution: Open video/image VLM with pooled crop/frame visual connector, structured packing, video pointing and long-context supervision.
Training methodology: Image pretraining 32k steps 60% captions/30% pointing/10% NLP; all parameters finetuned. Joint video/image SFT 30k steps, 16,384 length; long-context SFT 2k steps 36,864 length.
Compression mechanism: Multi-crop images, pooled frame windows, forward-attending visual tokens, timestamp interleaving; packed attention masks.
Relevance to our proposal: Connector architecture and question-following video robustness comparison.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Useful test for token policy preserving grounding under long video/image QA, but not direct adaptive-count prior art.
Experimental evidence (PDF pages): §4 pp.8–12; packing efficiency p.8; Table 7 p.12.
Question conditioning: Question influences supervised pointing output only, not visual token allocation.
Adaptive budget: Image crop count controlled by resolution and K (8 train/24 inference); video frame cap fixed; no learned per-question budget.
Frozen components: None in main stages: all parameters fine-tuned including ViT, connector, LLM.
Training objective: Caption/QA/pointing next-token SFT; no compute-aware reward.
Benchmarks: Video-MME; LongVideoBench; Molmo2-Track; Point-Bench; MeViS
Reported results: SFT message-tree packing averages 3.8 examples per 16,384-token sequence and reports 15× training efficiency. Image patch pooling is 2×2 versus 3×3 for video frames (methods p.6).
Limitations: Video-oriented; fixed compression, large contextual token cap, training all weights.

Paper title: Penguin-VL: Exploring the Efficiency Limits of VLM with LLM-based Vision Encoders
Primary contribution: Initialize visual encoder from text-only Qwen3-0.6B LLM; temporal redundancy-aware (TRA) visual budget prioritizes key frames over intermediate frames.
Training methodology: Vision initialization from language weights; vision feature reconstruction/relation objectives; joint multimodal alignment and SFT; video tokens bilinear downsampled after encoder.
Compression mechanism: If full tokens exceed Tmax, scale key/intermediate frames synchronously with ~16:1 token ratio; clamp intermediate frames at Tmin then continue scaling key frames; FFmpeg frame sampling capped at 180.
Relevance to our proposal: Adaptive token count under budget as image/video prior art.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Question-aware compute reward is distinct from question-agnostic temporal redundancy classification; compare static key-frame policy.
Question conditioning: No question conditioning of TRA: key/intermediate classification follows temporal similarity, not prompt relevance.
Adaptive budget: Yes: within global Tmax, adapt key-frame versus intermediate-frame resolutions based on temporal redundancy and minimum per-frame Tmin; not answer-driven.
Frozen components: Encoder initially inherits pretrained LLM weights, but stages jointly tune model; no persistent frozen decoder established.
Training objective: Multimodal generative/feature reconstruction learning; budget constraint is rule-based, not learned reward-minus-compute.
Benchmarks: DocVQA; ChartQA; InfoVQA; Video-MME; MVBench; LongVideoBench
Reported results: Penguin-Encoder 5-benchmark average 34.6 versus random-init 31.3 in Table 3. Penguin-VL-2B DocVQA 94.1, ChartQA 86.6, MVBench 65.5; Penguin-VL-8B DocVQA 96.2, MVBench 71.7 (Tables 1–2).
Limitations: TRA only for video temporal changes, potentially misses visually static but question-critical details; policy is heuristic; no decoder freezing.

Paper title: Unbundling Multimodal Vision Encoding
Research category: Token pruning and merging; Multimodal alignment and connector design; Vision encoder post-training; Supervised and differentiable compression
Primary contribution: Controlled matched-lifetime-compute study separates pretrained encoder prior, dedicated vision capacity, and whether capacity is placed before or inside multimodal decoder.
Training methodology: Trains all components from scratch for controlled lifetime compute; separate encoder-pretraining, text pretraining, multimodal training depending on recipe.
Compression mechanism: Early in-fusion vision-specific attention/FFN updates shared residual stream; matched total pretraining FLOPs across all stages.
Relevance to our proposal: Strong compute-accounting and visual capacity-location constraint.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Shows benefits of dedicated early vision processing; can inform whether connector policy capacity suffices when decoder is frozen.
Question conditioning: No question-conditioned image-token policy.
Adaptive budget: Token counts/compute budgets set by experimental protocols, not learned per query.
Frozen components: Frozen encoder analyzed as comparator; does not train frozen decoder under question-aware token reward.
Training objective: Matched lifetime training FLOPs and aggregate VQA/text scores; no token-cost regularized training reward.
Benchmarks: VQA category suite; OCR; vision-centric tasks; text benchmark suite
Reported results: At 1.7B backbone with 0.4B extra visual capacity, encoder-free avg VQA 39.0; scratch encoder 44.4; early (layers 1–8) vision-only FFN in-fusion 45.0; late (layers 21–28) 35.1 (Table 3). From-scratch joint encoder matches/exceeds MetaCLIP at matched lifetime compute (Fig.2).
Limitations: Models trained from scratch, not pretrained frozen looped VLM; study matches lifetime FLOPs rather than inference token cost.

Paper title: Molmo and PixMo: Open Weights and Open Data for State-of-the-Art Vision-Language Models
Primary contribution: High-resolution overlapping image crops, attentional patch pooling connector and human-authored PixMo data for strong open VLMs.
Training methodology: Pretrain on dense PixMo captions/pointing then task-mixed supervised fine-tuning; experiments with and without ViT finetuning.
Compression mechanism: Overlapping crop context avoids boundary artifacts; attention pooling of features from late ViT layers to LLM space.
Relevance to our proposal: High-resolution evaluation and connector baseline.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Counterpoint to aggressive compression; preserve patch-local OCR, spatial pointing under variable question budget.
Question conditioning: Question affects text supervision/pointing, not visual token count.
Adaptive budget: Number of crops selected as setup/resolution; no question-conditioned learned budget.
Frozen components: Not generally frozen: encoder finetuning and dropout/tuning options ablated; LLM trained.
