Benchmarks: DocVQA; ChartQA; TextVQA; MMMU; AI2D; PixMo-Count; human preference
Reported results: Molmo-7B-D 11-task average 77.3 and Elo 1056; Molmo-72B 81.2 and Elo 1077 in Table 1. Crop ablation 4 train/4 test 11-avg 71.0 versus 36 train/36 test 77.2 (Table 2b).
Limitations: More crops improve detail while raising token and encoder compute; no sample-specific question-aware compression.

Paper title: LoopZip: Visual Token Compression for Efficient Looped Vision-Language Models
Research category: Adaptive visual token compression; Question-conditioned vision encoding; Token pruning and merging; Looped and recurrent transformers
Primary contribution: Training-free, cross-invocation-aware visual compression for genuinely weight-shared looped VLM backbones.
Training methodology: No parameter training or fine-tuning; per-example analytic value correction at inference.
Compression mechanism: Direct salient-patch retention plus similarity-group summaries; average instruction attention across two weight-tied invocations; regularized joint least-squares correction of retained visual value vectors against both full-pool attention outputs, applied at second call only; subsequently shortened sequence and native cached decoding.
Relevance to our proposal: Closest direct prior art: frozen true looped VLM plus question-conditioned token selection; a trainable, query-conditioned visual module and learned compute-aware budget must demonstrably add something beyond this training-free cross-call baseline.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Direct novelty collision on cross-invocation visual compression; explicit comparator for latency, quality and token schedule.
Method evidence (PDF pages): PDF pp.2–5, §§3.1–4.5, Figs.2–6, Algorithm 1 and Eq.(6)
Question conditioning: Yes: instruction-to-image attention averaged over first two calls selects retained candidates; initial aggregation is image-attention/feature-similarity based.
Adaptive budget: No learned per-question budget/halting: target average pruning ratio is supplied; K0/K1 scheduled to match it, with fixed two-call observation.
Frozen components: Entire pretrained looped VLM (vision encoder, projector, shared language backbone); weights and schedule unchanged.
Training objective: At inference, minimize mean squared discrepancy between compressed and original attention outputs at selected instruction query positions over two calls, plus lambda times squared Frobenius norm of value correction; no task-loss or compute-aware training objective.
Benchmarks: MMStar; RealWorldQA; VMCB; AI2D; ChartQA; HRBench4K; POPE; HallusionBench; MMMU-Pro; MathVista; LogicVista
Reported results: Table 1, p.6: at 50% average pruning LoopVL-1B mean 59.02 vs uncompressed 60.58 (97.16% relative); SenseNova-Loop-9B-Preview 67.65 vs 70.21 (96.02%). At 87.5% pruning, LoopVL retention 83.89% vs VisionZip 80.06% (p.7). At 8192 original visual tokens/87.5% pruning on H20, HF/vLLM/SGLang end-to-end speedups 2.01/2.47/2.02x and memory reductions 58.98/58.41/58.36% (p.7, Fig.8). Component ablation full 56.53 vs no cross-call selection 55.45 and no joint fitting 55.17 on three-benchmark average (p.7, Table 2); two observations 56.53 vs six 55.36 with compression time 42.05 vs 95.67 ms (p.8, Table 3).
Limitations: Assumes accessible attention and first-two-call intermediate outputs; requires an already looped backbone; fixed pruning ratio rather than input-adaptive allocation; per-example fitting overhead; changing importance across still later calls only approximated.
Warnings: Do not confuse compression of visual tokens in a looped backbone with a learned loop controller. Results are within reported hardware/framework/prompt conditions; 97.16% is relative mean performance, not absolute accuracy.

Paper title: Looping Back to Move Forward: Recursive Transformers for Efficient and Flexible Large Multimodal Models
Research category: Multimodal alignment and connector design; Looped and recurrent transformers; Adaptive computation and reasoning depth
Primary contribution: RecursiveVLM reuses full decoder layer weights across multimodal refinement passes and stabilizes feedback with separate visual/text multi-layer connectors and per-step monotonic supervision.
Training methodology: Continued pretraining on 6M multimodal plus 3M text samples, then SFT on Data1 (9M multimodal QA +3M text) or Data2 (8M long-CoT +2.6M text); AdamW and R=2, per-step beta=1.5; paper does not specify a frozen decoder during this training.
Compression mechanism: Full multimodal hidden states pass through modality-specific multi-layer feedback connector, summed with initial modality embeddings; same decoder weights are executed again and predictions can be read at intermediate recursion depths.
Relevance to our proposal: Direct genuine looped multimodal backbone and depth-supervision reference; useful comparator and motivation for a frozen-decoder, vision-only adaptive controller with explicit compute cost.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Separates demonstrated benefit of recursive decoder computation from visual-token reduction and learned budget allocation.
Question conditioning: Questions are standard model inputs; no explicit query-conditioned visual compression/router.
Adaptive budget: Supports evaluation at one or two passes after training at R=2; no learned per-query stop policy or compute penalty. R=3 ablated rather than input-conditioned.
Frozen components: No frozen decoder or encoder claimed; pretrained initialization and shared parameters are not freezing.
Training objective: Sum of token cross-entropy across all recursion steps; multiply a token's step-r CE by beta=1.5 if it exceeds previous-step CE (monotonic recursion loss). No measured FLOP/latency penalty.
Benchmarks: AI2D; MMStar; MMVet; MMMU; MMBench; MathVista; OCRBench; HallusionBench
Reported results: PDF p.6 Table 1: Data1 standard R=1 benchmark average 55.31, vanilla recursion R=2 evaluated at second pass 50.15, RecursiveVLM first/second pass 57.46/58.86. Data2 standard 58.60 vs RecursiveVLM first/second 59.52/62.60. PDF p.8 Table 6: HallusionBench 37.56/38.69/45.12 at 1/2/3 passes, while MMStar 45.03/52.10/51.07: more passes do not uniformly improve general reasoning. Table 5 p.8: per-step monotonic objective first/second AI2D 72.57/74.64 vs final-only 68.85/72.02.
Limitations: Requires training/continued pretraining of a large multimodal backbone; adds entire decoder pass per step; no visual-token cost control; single optimum R=2 on many general tasks and no automatic per-instance stop; no measured efficiency/latency versus accuracy in main table.
Warnings: Authors call inference flexible/depth-adaptive, but evaluation at different manually selected R is not a learned adaptive-budget controller; the recurrence is in the language backbone, not solely vision.

Paper title: Less is More: Recursive Reasoning with Tiny Networks
Primary contribution: TRM simplifies HRM to one weight-shared two-layer tiny network recursively updating latent reasoning and proposed answer, with deep supervision and a lightweight correctness-based halt head.
Training methodology: Supervised puzzle-grid training with heavy augmentation; one full recursion cycle differentiated per supervision step, EMA improves stability; T=3,n=6 strong Sudoku configuration.
Compression mechanism: Shared net repeatedly updates z=net(x,y,z), y=net(y,z), carries detached states between deep-supervision steps; binary Q head triggers halt when predicted answer correct.
Relevance to our proposal: Conceptual template for detached iterations, step supervision and cheap halting, but not direct precedent for looped generative VLM or frozen decoder.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Relevant to compute-aware stopping and recurrent latent reasoning only, not image-language token routing.
Method evidence (PDF pages): PDF pp.3–7, §§2.4–4.8, Fig.3 pseudocode and Tables 1–3
Question conditioning: Input puzzle x participates in latent update; not natural-language question-guided visual selection.
Adaptive budget: Yes, supervision-step ACT-style early stopping from a Q head trained to predict answer correctness, but no per-visual-token or decoder-loop budget optimization.
Frozen components: No pretrained/frozen language decoder, image encoder or multimodal stack.
Training objective: Answer cross-entropy plus BCE on correctness/halting probability, at deep-supervision steps; no explicit FLOP penalty.
Benchmarks: Sudoku-Extreme; Maze-Hard; ARC-AGI-1; ARC-AGI-2
Reported results: PDF p.5 Table 1: Sudoku-Extreme 87.4% for 5M TRM-MLP vs HRM 55.0% at 27M; single-feature variant 71.9% vs two-feature 87.4% (p.6 Table 2). PDF p.8 Tables 4–5: 7M attention TRM Maze-Hard 85.3% vs HRM 74.5%; ARC-AGI-1/2 44.6%/7.8% vs HRM 40.3%/5.0% (2 tries). Adding ACT variant scored 86.1% vs no-extra-forward-pass alternative 87.4% Sudoku (p.5 Table 1, p.7 §4.6).
Limitations: Deterministic non-generative supervised puzzle solver; grid-specific and augmentation-heavy; costly recursion/OOM at greater depth; halting tied to answer correctness, no visual tokens or VLM.
Warnings: Exact byte-identical PDF duplicate of id 41 (matching manifest SHA-256 c2b3ef5a8d6bc68e667aa01e8405dcfd9ebe88cfe1c6e58f04c5a6d652ce7af9); count as one work. Abstract rounds ARC to 45%/8%, tables specify 44.6%/7.8%.

Paper title: Less is More: Recursive Reasoning with Tiny Networks
Primary contribution: TRM; identical paper to id 40, not an independent paper or independent result.
Training methodology: Same small supervised puzzle datasets/augmentations as id 40.
Compression mechanism: Recursive latent and answer updates with detached earlier cycles and one differentiated final cycle.
Relevance to our proposal: One duplicate copy of TRM for halting/latent recursion context.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Excluded duplicate copy (byte-identical to PDF ID 040). Original study retains its own priority.
Method evidence (PDF pages): PDF pp.3–7, §§2.4–4.8, Fig.3; exactly matches id 40

Reported results: Identical to id 40: PDF p.8 Tables 4–5 report Sudoku 87.4% (TRM-MLP), Maze 85.3% and ARC-AGI-1/2 44.6%/7.8% (TRM-Att); not a replication.

Paper title: Qwen2-VL: Enhancing Vision-Language Model’s Perception of the World at Any Resolution
Primary contribution: Native dynamic-resolution images, M-RoPE temporal/height/width and unified image/video handling.
Training methodology: Three stages: vision training, all-parameter multimodal training, then ViT locked and language instruction fine-tuned; 600B plus 800B pretraining tokens, text-token next-token supervision.
Compression mechanism: Dynamic image sizing preserves aspect ratio, 2D positional representation and visual-token sequence; variable token count is input-size based.
Relevance to our proposal: Open baseline and demonstration that variable visual-token input length matters, not evidence of learned iterative compute.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Distinguish native image resolution budgets from learned adaptive loop or task-dependent visual compute.
Question conditioning: No: image-native resolution/token bounds rather than query-selected visual budget.
Adaptive budget: Variable image tokens per native resolution; no learned question-dependent token count or adaptive decoder loops.
Frozen components: ViT frozen only in final instruction stage; decoder trained rather than held permanently frozen.
Training objective: Autoregressive text token supervision; no compute-aware token/loop penalty.
Benchmarks: MMMU; DocVQA; InfoVQA; RealWorldQA; OCRBench; AI2D; ChartQA; MMStar; MathVista; Video-MME
Reported results: PDF p.9 Table 2: Qwen2-VL-72B MMMU-val 64.5, DocVQA-test 96.5 and MMStar 68.3. PDF p.14 Table 7: Qwen2-VL-7B dynamic average 1,924 image tokens with InfoVQA-val 75.89 and OCRBench 866; fixed 3,136 tokens gives InfoVQA 77.27 but OCRBench 786, indicating no fixed resolution dominates.
Limitations: Resolution adaptivity not conditioned on semantic question; trained full backbone; visual compute still rises with input size.
Warnings: Do not interpret per-image native resolution variation as trained question-aware adaptive budget.

Paper title: InternVL3.5: Advancing Open-Source Multimodal Models in Versatility, Reasoning, and Efficiency
Research category: Adaptive visual token compression; Multimodal alignment and connector design; Vision encoder post-training; Supervised and differentiable compression; Knowledge distillation; Adaptive computation and reasoning depth
Primary contribution: InternVL3.5-Flash adds patch-level binary Visual Resolution Router (ViR), trained with output-consistency labels to pick 256 versus 64 visual tokens per image tile; pipeline separation (DvD) boosts serving throughput.
Training methodology: Main model pretraining ~250B tokens, SFT ~130B, Cascade RL; ViCO consistency trains full model with frozen reference; subsequent router-only training uses OCR/VQA-heavy SFT subset and CE with percentile threshold.
Compression mechanism: ViCO stage 1 jointly adjusts MLLM against frozen full-resolution teacher via response-distribution KL under 256/64-token views; stage 2 computes compression-induced loss ratio and trains binary ViR on labels, freezing ViT/projector/LLM.
Relevance to our proposal: Strongest direct antecedent for trainable frozen-backbone visual-budget controller and KL teacher consistency; target novelty must add explicit query conditioning, loop-aware multi-step scoring and compute-aware joint budget.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Potential novelty collision on training vision router while freezing rest; precise stage separation changes claim of frozen decoder.
Question conditioning: Router evaluates patch semantic richness/visual information; no explicit question-text conditioning in ViR classifier documented. KL targets derive from response, so training signal is task-dependent although routing mechanism is not explicitly query-conditioned.
Adaptive budget: Yes, learned per-tile binary visual token budget, with threshold based on historical KL/loss ratios; not learned number of decoder loops.
Frozen components: In router-training stage, entire ViT, MLP and decoder frozen; frozen teacher during preceding consistency stage, where policy MLLM is updated.
Training objective: Teacher/policy KL between 256-token reference and randomly 256/64-token policy responses; binary CE for loss-ratio-based router. No decoder-loop compute-aware loss.
Benchmarks: DocVQA; ChartVQA; InfoVQA; TextVQA; OCRBench; AI2D; MMStar; MMMU; MathVista; MathVision; MathVerse; DynaMath
Reported results: PDF p.24 Table 17: 8B nine-benchmark average 80.2 baseline vs 79.8 Flash, 38B 83.9 vs 83.4; p.4 reports ~50% fewer visual tokens. PDF p.24 Table 18: at 896 resolution/16 req/s, 38B throughput 2.71 baseline, 5.06 DvD, 10.97 DvD+ViR requests/s (4.05x combined, NOT ViR alone); p.23 Table 15 8B reasoning aggregate 53.6 instruct, 56.3 MPO, 60.3 CascadeRL.
Limitations: Binary routing granularity and image-semantic rather than explicitly question-aware; consistency phase unfreezes main decoder; visual-token compression after ViT does not save ViT computations; no recurrent weight-tied backbone or loop halting; combined DvD+ViR speedups must not be credited entirely to ViR.
Warnings: Table 17 uses abbreviated 235B-MoE naming while architecture Table 1 calls full model 241B-A28B; do not conflate with model size. 4.05x throughput is DvD+ViR over baseline at 896 on 38B, not router-only.

Paper title: Qwen2.5-VL Technical Report
Primary contribution: Windowed ViT attention and native dynamic resolution/video frame rate, 2x2 visual-feature merger before LLM.
Training methodology: ViT-only visual pretrain 1.5T tokens, joint ViT+LLM multimodal pretrain 2T, long-context joint pretrain 0.6T (total 4.1T); SFT/DPO posttrain with frozen ViT.
Compression mechanism: Window attention reduces ViT quadratic load; spatial merger reduces downstream sequence length fourfold; temporal M-RoPE aligned to absolute timestamps.
Relevance to our proposal: Strong off-the-shelf non-looping VLM baseline/encoder design; duplicated as manifest id 30.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Compare trained visual frontend and standard decoder cost to looped approach.
Experimental evidence (PDF pages): PDF pp.11–14, §3, Table 3 and video benchmark tables
Question conditioning: No learned task/question-aware visual selection; standard prompt conditions decoder.
Adaptive budget: Resolution/fps-dependent tokens, not trained per-question budget or recursive depth.
Frozen components: LLM initialized pretrained but trained jointly after first stage; ViT frozen in SFT and DPO, not decoder.
Training objective: Text next-token prediction and SFT/DPO; no resource-regularized visual selection or loop supervision.
Benchmarks: MMMU; MMMU-Pro; MathVista; MATH-Vision; MMStar; DocVQA; OCRBench; Video-MME
Reported results: PDF p.11 Table 3: Qwen2.5-VL-72B MMMU-val 70.2, MMMU-Pro 51.1, MMStar 70.8 and MathVista-mini 74.8; 7B MMMU-val 58.6 and MMStar 63.9. PDF p.8 Table 2 specifies 1.5T/2T/0.6T tokens across three phases.
Limitations: No frozen decoder posttraining, learned question-aware budget or true looping; image-token merger is fixed.
Warnings: Manifest id 44 file is byte-identical to id 30 (same SHA-256 399a28f6ed79f4ece29cca93993fceb56fc304b1d779e49392aec05aff45aba5); avoid counting as a separate work.

Paper title: Qwen3-VL Technical Report
Primary contribution: DeepStack injects multi-depth ViT visual features into first three decoder layers without growing language context length; thinking variants use generated CoT and posttraining.
Training methodology: S0 merger-only 67B tokens freezes ViT and LLM; S1 full-parameter ~1T at 8K, S2 full-parameter ~1T at 32K, S3 100B at 256K; SFT, distillation and RL after pretrain.
Compression mechanism: Three distinct ViT feature levels separately projected into first three LLM layers via DeepStack; interleaved multimodal RoPE and textual timestamps.
Relevance to our proposal: Important multi-layer visual-injection baseline and caution that increased visual feature channels need not increase input token count.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Compare mechanism with proposed looped frozen decoder and budget-aware visual frontend.
Method evidence (PDF pages): PDF pp.2–5, §§2.1–3.1, Fig.1 and pretraining schedule
Question conditioning: Standard input question and autoregressive thinking only; no explicit query-conditioned visual token router.
Adaptive budget: Thinking vs instruct variants and generated CoT can alter output-token compute; no learned per-image vision or internal loop budget.
Frozen components: Both encoder and decoder frozen only in initial merger-alignment stage; not throughout training.
Training objective: Autoregressive next-token text/CoT supervision with token reweighting and posttraining objectives; no adaptive visual-loop compute regularization.
Benchmarks: MMStar; MMMU-Pro; MathVista; MathVision; OCRBench; Video-MME; LongVideoBench
Reported results: PDF p.15 Table 2: Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Thinking MMStar 78.7 and MMMU-Pro 69.3 (read Thinking column); PDF p.4 pretraining schedule S0 67B, S1 ~1T, S2 ~1T, S3 100B tokens; comparisons of model sizes/instruct-vs-thinking in pp.13–24. Results depend on benchmark and reasoning mode.
Limitations: Training full LLM at scale; DeepStack modifies decoder representations/layers, contrary to permanently frozen decoder; no repeated shared-layer invocations or token budget policy.
Warnings: Paper title page dated December 1, 2025 (arXiv header Nov 27, 2025); classify as 2025. DeepStack's multiple LLM layer injections are NOT looped decoder execution.

Paper title: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: Pushing the Limits of KV Cache Compression
Primary contribution: CED/CSA2 and FP4 reduce agentic prefill and KV storage; native vision pathway uses 3x3 pixel-unshuffle; scalar effort controls output reasoning expenditure.
Training methodology: Vision encoder trained from scratch, contrastive then autoregressive 236B-token visual fine-tuning; vision frozen initially during main pretraining except final norm/projector, later unfrozen at learning-rate decay; model undergoes broad multimodal pretraining and agentic RL.
Compression mechanism: DeepSeek-ViT variable-resolution 2D-RoPE, modality-specific expert load biases, 3x3 pixel-unshuffle; CSA2 sparse KV reuse; CED prefill/decode asymmetry; effort-conditioned posttraining.
Relevance to our proposal: Contrast frontier notion of compute budget (reasoning-output effort and cache) with internal learned looped vision compute; efficient visual-front-end merger baseline.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Shows effort control alone is not the same mechanism as loop-count/visual-token allocation.
Method evidence (PDF pages): PDF pp.7–14, §§2.1–2.5; pp.21–23, §4.2; p.30 effort interface
Experimental evidence (PDF pages): PDF pp.23–24 and 33–37, §§4.3,6, Table 1 and limitations
Question conditioning: Vision pixels and text are jointly input; not a learned question-aware vision module.
Adaptive budget: Public max/high/low scalar b=100/75/50 steers generated reasoning effort/output token budget, not visual token budget or number of repeated weight-shared passes.
Frozen components: Vision encoder frozen during early main pretraining, later unfrozen; language backbone not a permanently frozen training target.
Training objective: Vision sigmoid contrastive and next-token prediction phases; downstream token and RL/reasoning-effort objectives; no loss jointly constraining vision-loop budget.
Benchmarks: MMMU-Pro; DocVQA; CVBench; RefCOCO; MMLU-Pro; LongBench-V2; DeepSWE; Terminal-Bench
Reported results: PDF p.24 Table 1 base model MMMU-Pro 56.5 (4-shot), CVBench 77.9, DocVQA 95.6 and RefCOCO-average 86.0; earlier DeepSeek-V4 baselines lack these multimodal numbers, so no direct multimodal improvement claim from the table. PDF p.37: 890 bytes/token global KV, ~1/4 previous V4-Flash, persistent KV ~1/8; p.30 maps effort tiers to b=100/75/50.
Limitations: Extreme scale, large pretraining/RL and cache-heavy design; fixed 9x visual merger, no looped decoder steps or query-conditioned visual budget; note robustness boundaries on sparse selection and cache reconstruction.
Warnings: Not a looped VLM merely because KV is reused across layers or agents reason iteratively; do not mistake external agent/tool cycles for shared decoder recursions.

Compression mechanism: Frozen patch-based encoders on most variants; 12B direct patch projection; local/global attention and KV reuse reduce context costs, not repeated decoder passes.
Relevance to our proposal: Shows fixed-budget 280-vs-1120 visual token trade-off and multimodal baseline, but frozen component is opposite to target (encoder rather than decoder).
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Guard against citing frozen encoder as evidence for frozen decoder training.

Adaptive budget: Preset visual resolution and optional thinking text generation, not per-query learned loop/token budget.
Frozen components: ViT and audio encoders frozen during pretraining for encoder-based variants; decoder remains trainable. 12B has no separate encoder to freeze.
Training objective: Autoregressive language modeling and thinking-trace training; no explicit compute-aware looped-vision objective.
Benchmarks: MMMU Pro; MATH-Vision; InfographicVQA; OmniDocBench 1.5; MMLU Pro; AIME 2026
Reported results: PDF p.6 Table 6 at maximal 1120 vision tokens with thinking: MMMU Pro E2B/E4B/12B/26B-A4B/31B = 44.2/52.6/69.1/73.8/76.9; MATH-Vision same order 52.4/59.5/79.7/82.4/85.6.
