Warnings: Do not equate key/value cache reuse, speculative draft steps or textual thinking with weight-shared recurrent VLM passes. PDF title page date June 19, 2026; arXiv v2 header July 24, 2026.

Paper title: Kimi K3: Open Frontier Intelligence Technical Report
Primary contribution: Native from-scratch multimodal MoE with Kimi Delta Attention recurrent sequence state, attention residuals and 2x2 vision pixel shuffle; effort-conditioned multi-domain agentic RL.
Training methodology: Joint language-vision pretraining from start with text and visual tokens under next-token prediction; 8K to 64K pretraining then 256K to 1M extension, per-head Muon; posttraining RL and on-policy distillation.
Compression mechanism: KDA recurrent state propagates along token sequence within a layer; MLA layers offer global retrieval, AttnRes mixes across layer outputs; MoonViT trained from scratch via native next-token objective.
Relevance to our proposal: Explicit taxonomy counterexample: sequence-state recurrence and external reasoning/action loops are not the proposed repeated shared decoder on the same question/image.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Avoid claiming KDA or agent tool use as evidence of internal looped-VLM compute scaling.
Question conditioning: No query-specific visual token selector; visual input joins autoregressive stream and agents can inspect screens in external tool loop.
Adaptive budget: Several output reasoning-effort levels; not learned visual tokens per query or repeated same-backbone decoder iterations.
Frozen components: No frozen decoder or frozen vision encoder in native training; an EAGLE-style speculative draft stage freezes target model but is separate from visual-token training.
Training objective: Autoregressive NTP with multimodal data and subsequent RL/effort objectives; no loss on decoder-loop count or question-specific visual-token cost.
Benchmarks: WorldVQA; OmniDocBench; PerceptionBench; Video-MME; MMMU-Pro; Math-Vision; ZeroBench; GPQA Diamond; Terminal-Bench 2.1
Reported results: PDF p.11 Table 1: 2.78T total/104.2B active, 401M ViT, 69 KDA+24 MLA; PDF pp.27–28 Table 2: WorldVQA 51.0, OmniDocBench 91.1, Terminal-Bench 2.1 88.3 under max effort; p.26 notes MMMU-Pro/Math-Vision cells vary with Python tools, so tool-aided and unaided figures should not be conflated.
Limitations: Compute/parameter scale prohibitive for small frozen-decoder research; fixed 4x visual pooling; no inner recurrent pass of entire VLM despite recurrent attention and vision-in-the-loop agent use.
Warnings: Report uses 'vision-in-the-loop' for agentic observation/action, not full weight-shared VLM decoder passes. Scores under max effort and sometimes external tools.

Paper title: On the Design of Qwen3.8-Next Architecture: Evaluation, Efficiency, and Training Stability
Primary contribution: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next combines Gated DeltaNet token recurrence, sparse global attention, gated residual branches, n-gram off-device embeddings and Muon for text-model efficiency.
Training methodology: Text-centric pretraining architectural ablations on 25B-A3B models (400B tokens 4K +80B tokens 32K); Flash-Next production model trained with Muon and gated residuals.
Compression mechanism: GDN updates finite-dimensional state along the token/time axis inside individual layers; QSA retrieves selected long-context blocks; no repeated whole-decoder invocation on the same hidden states.
Relevance to our proposal: Negative control for terminology: GDN recurrence, sparse token-index and branched residuals must not be misrepresented as looped VLM.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Useful architecture caution only; no direct frozen-decoder visual compute baseline.
Method evidence (PDF pages): PDF pp.1–5 and 8–16, §§1–2, Figs.1 and GDN state Eqs.(1)–(5)
Question conditioning: Text prompts condition token attention normally; no visual question module.
Adaptive budget: No question-conditioned visual or loop-count budget; sparse indexer chooses context micro-blocks.
Frozen components: No frozen VLM decoder or trained vision module described.
Training objective: Next-token training loss and downstream evaluations; compute/throughput engineering but no looped-VLM quality-cost objective.
Benchmarks: MMLU; MMLU-Pro; SuperGPQA; MATH; GSM8K; BBH; EvalPlus; MultiPL-E; RULER; MRCR
Reported results: PDF p.5 Table 1: matched 25B-A3B GDN hybrid average 53.81 vs SWA hybrid 51.15 and full-attention 49.87 over nine text benchmarks. PDF p.8 Table 2: QSA average 76.8 vs full attention 75.9 on eight text tasks; Table 3 at 1M MRCR 26.44 vs 20.71. PDF p.23 Table 11: 125B total/6B active/51B n-gram, MMLU-Pro 73.23 vs Qwen3.7-Plus 70.90, but MATH 72.78 vs 74.38.
Limitations: Explicitly not a multimodal/vision model in this report; recurrent *sequence* attention does not establish recursive model-depth reasoning or compression across VLM calls.
Warnings: Filename 2026_Qwen3.8-Next.pdf abbreviates actual title; abstract names Qwen3.8-Flash-Next. MMMLU is a multilingual textual benchmark, NOT MMMU multimodal.

Paper title: SparseVLM: Visual Token Sparsification for Efficient Vision-Language Model Inference
Research category: Adaptive visual token compression; Question-conditioned vision encoding; Token pruning and merging
Primary contribution: Question-guided, training-free progressive decoder pruning with selected text raters, attention-matrix-rank-dependent number of deletions, and density-peak aggregation of selected discarded tokens.
Training methodology: None: no added parameters or fine-tuning; all components taken from pretrained VLM, with heuristic λ, τ, θ.
Compression mechanism: Rank-dependent prune lowest text-to-vision attention; recycle the top-τ fraction of deleted tokens by kNN density peaks (ρ_iδ_i) into θ-fraction cluster centers and sum group tokens (Eqs. 8–10). Appendix B describes dual FlashAttention passes to recover pruning signals.
Relevance to our proposal: Direct precedent for text-guided, input-dependent token deletion with frozen pretrained VLM, but not a trained vision-side RL policy or proactive pre-decoder token-count controller.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: P1: covers question conditioning plus adaptive decoder-layer sparsity and frozen weights, but compression location/training differ from target.
Method evidence (PDF pages): PDF pp. 3–4, §3.1–3.3, Eqs. 2–10; PDF p. 5, §3.4, Eq. 11; PDF pp. 12–14, Appendix B–C (FlashAttention and overhead)
Experimental evidence (PDF pages): PDF p. 6, Tables 1–2; PDF p. 7, Table 3 and §4.2; PDF p. 8, Table 4 and §5.3
Question conditioning: Yes. Select prompt text raters using average softmax of visual-embedding/text-embedding similarities above the mean (Eqs. 5–6); their language-query to visual-key decoder attention gives each image token importance (Eqs. 2–3).
Adaptive budget: Per-layer removal N_l=λ[L_v−rank(P_l)] (Eq. 7); varies with input/attention rank and can skip a layer. λ, recycling fractions and evaluation retained-token targets are prescribed, not a learned per-question cost/accuracy stopping policy; reported LLaVA configurations 192/128/64 of 576.
Frozen components: Original vision encoder, projector and decoder parameters unchanged (training-free); runtime decoder hidden-state/token sequence modified.
Training objective: No training loss. Inference importance P=A[text raters,vision], mean across raters; delete λ(L_v−rank P) lowest importance tokens, reconstruct chosen dropped tokens by sum; Eq. 11 estimates saved FLOPs net of scoring and clustering overhead.
Benchmarks: GQA; MMBench; MME; POPE; ScienceQA; SEED-Bench; TextVQA; MM-Vet; TGIF-QA; MSVD-QA; MSRVTT-QA; ActivityNet-QA
Reported results: LLaVA-1.5-7B Table 1: 576 full tokens average normalized score 100%, 4.62 TFLOPs, latency 57.82 ms; at 192 tokens SparseVLM 99.1%, 2.14 TFLOPs, 36.50 ms; at 128 tokens 96.7%, 1.72 TFLOPs, 33.28 ms; at 64 tokens 89.3%, 1.30 TFLOPs, 29.89 ms (PDF p. 6, Table 1).; At 128 tokens LLaVA GQA 58.4 vs full 61.9, POPE 85.0 vs 85.9, TextVQA 56.7 vs 58.3; 64-token POPE 77.5 vs full 85.9 (PDF p. 6, Table 1).; Qwen2-VL Table 2 dynamic baseline mean 83.7 (MMB 80.5/1323 tokens, POPE 86.4/1311, TextVQA 84.3/1326); at 600 tokens mean 82.1 (PDF p. 6, Table 2).; Video-LLaVA 2048→194 total vision tokens: mean accuracy 47.0 versus full 47.9 and FastV 40.5; normalized 95.0% vs FastV 80.3%; first 1000 samples per video benchmark (PDF p. 7, Table 3 and §4.2).; Token recycling ablation at 64 tokens raises GQA 52.2→53.8 and POPE 72.8→77.5 (PDF p. 8, Table 4).
Limitations: Still computes full vision encoder and enters decoder before pruning; no vision-side RL or learned cost-aware stopping.; Reported fixed token target comparisons must not be conflated with unconstrained per-sample budget optimization.; Rank/SVD and recycling add overhead and runtime FlashAttention workaround uses two passes; savings depend on setup.
Warnings: Paper prose p. 8 says 43.1% CUDA reduction and 62.8% FLOPs at 128 tokens; Table 1 reports 57.82→33.28 ms and 4.62→1.72 TFLOPs: treat Table 1 columns/metrics as source of numerical comparison rather than equating latency with CUDA time.

Paper title: AdaptVision: Efficient Vision-Language Models via Adaptive Visual Acquisition
Research category: Adaptive visual token compression; Question-conditioned vision encoding; Reinforcement learning for visual token optimization; Adaptive computation and reasoning depth
Primary contribution: RL-trained policy examines low-resolution image/question, directly answers easy samples or calls a bounding-box crop tool once for extra high-resolution visual tokens; DTPO separates tool and answer optimization with area-aware reward.
Training methodology: RL fine-tuning of policy/Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct with veRL on VisionThink-Smart-Train VQA samples; 16 sampled rollouts/prompt, batch 512, mini-batch 32, AdamW 1e-6 for 80 steps on 32 H20 GPUs, no KL term in implemented training (Appendix A.2). GPT-4o judges answer correctness and crop relevance; Qwen3-VL-4B judge variant tested.
Compression mechanism: Single coarse-to-fine tool-use decision; 1/4-resolution image then optionally high-resolution crop. Accuracy/format/balance reward plus crop-correctness and relative area penalty. DTPO separates normalization for tool vs answer tokens and group-relative advantages A_oc and A_tool.
Relevance to our proposal: Closest task-level threat to adaptive question-conditioned number of vision tokens trained with RL. Different implementation and training boundary: active VLM/tool policy rather than frozen decoder and vision-side selector in a looped VLM.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: P0: already formulates minimal per-example visual token use and trains with RL and cost-sensitive reward.
Method evidence (PDF pages): PDF pp. 3–4, Fig. 2 and §4.1, Eq. 5 (token count); PDF pp. 4–5, §4.2–4.3, Eqs. 6–14 (reward/DTPO); PDF p. 11, Appendix A.2 (optimizer and hardware); PDF p. 12, Appendix G (turn limit)
Experimental evidence (PDF pages): PDF p. 6, Table 1, §5.1–5.2; PDF p. 7, Figs. 4–6; PDF p. 11, Fig. 9 and Appendix A.2; PDF p. 12, Table 3
Question conditioning: Yes: model decides to crop based on low-resolution image and question, and predicts a question-relevant bounding box.
Adaptive budget: Actual per-example tokens depend on whether tool called and predicted crop size, with first-view ~25% of full-resolution tokens. Reward penalizes unnecessary tool calls and overly broad correct crops; one crop interaction, not arbitrary patch mask.
Frozen components: Paper does not document a frozen language decoder or vision-only updates; trains the policy model. The reference in standard GRPO equations is not evidence that deployed Qwen decoder is frozen.
Training objective: R=R_oc+R_tool; R_oc=R_acc+R_form+R_bal (binary correctness judge, 0.5 format reward, 0.1 balance penalties); R_tool=R_crop−αR_area (α=2); R_area=1(correct answer and crop)·clip(r_a/μ_a−1,0,1), with r_a=crop area/low-image area. Group-relative advantage for direct answer A_oc+λA_tool, for tool response A_oc+λA_tool on tool tokens and A_oc on answer tokens (λ=0.3); DTPO Eq. 12 separately normalizes group tool and answer token policy terms, clipped PPO/GRPO token loss Eq. 2. Implementation drops KL.
Benchmarks: ChartQA; OCRBench; DocVQA; MME; MM-Vet; RealWorldQA; POPE; MathVista; MathVerse
Reported results: Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct 9-benchmark Table 1: AdaptVision 33% mean visual token use and 97.9% mean normalized performance vs full 100%/100%, downsample 25%/92.1%, VisionThink reproduced 52%/95.8%, and without DTPO 57%/96.7% (PDF p. 6, Table 1).; AdaptVision ChartQA 75.92 vs full 79.8; OCRBench 76.9 vs 81.5; MME 2379 vs 2316; MM-Vet 64.8 vs 61.6; MathVerse 42.3 vs 46.3 (PDF p. 6, Table 1).; Paper reports 1.67× overall speedup relative to vanilla, with inference-time comparison across nine datasets (PDF pp. 6–7, Fig. 4 and §5.2).; Illustrative tool example uses 414 initial + 66 crop visual tokens, versus 1658 in full Qwen; recovers correct motorcycle number where low-res-only fails (PDF p. 11, Fig. 9).
Limitations: Requires explicit tool-turn generation and second visual encoder pass on hard queries, incurring latency; one crop only in evaluated system (Appendix G).; No frozen-decoder / vision-side-only optimization evidence; policy fine-tuning and expensive external judges/train hardware.; Average 33% token use, not a guarantee of minimum per-sample tokens; cropping is coarse region acquisition, not learned per-patch pruning on existing full encoded image.; Official VisionThink† released model uses ~99% tokens, reproduced variant 52%; their comparison must preserve this distinction (PDF pp. 6–7).
Warnings: R_area uses group mean of crop sizes from correct-answer/correct-crop rollouts; sample-specific budget is implicit via crop size, not an explicit learned integer K.; The 1/4-resolution and 25% token claim is paper terminology; exact pixel/resizing rule should not be inferred from it.

Paper title: CRISP: Pre-LLM Yet Text-Driven Visual Token Pruning for Efficient LVLM Inference
Research category: Question-conditioned vision encoding; Token pruning and merging
Primary contribution: Pre-decoder training-free two-stage selector: noun-conditioned cosine relevance allocates critical tokens per word, then greedy max-min feature diversity fills the remaining fixed budget.
Training methodology: None; no learned weights or additional fine-tuning. Noun extractor is pretrained 12 MB spaCy model; hyperparameters manually set.
Compression mechanism: S_ij=cos(v_i,e_j) (Eq. 2); noun j quota proportional to sum CLS attention of its most relevant image tokens (Eq. 3); select union of per-noun top-ranked tokens (Eq. 4), then iteratively add remaining token with minimum maximum cosine similarity to current selected set until K (Eq. 5).
Relevance to our proposal: Strong cheap pre-LLM, query-aware frozen-backbone baseline; substantial novelty overlap for text-image cosine ranking, word-conditioned quotas and complement-by-diversity, but no learned variable K.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: P1: directly threatens query-aware pre-decoder selection but not adaptive total token count/vision-side RL.
Method evidence (PDF pages): PDF pp. 2–3, Fig. 3 and §III.A–C, Eqs. 1–5; PDF p. 3, §IV.A (noun model and α)
Experimental evidence (PDF pages): PDF p. 4, Table I; PDF p. 5, Tables II–IV and §IV.B–D
Question conditioning: Yes: regex strip instructions, spaCy en_core_web_sm extracts nouns; average subword text embeddings, cosine with each projected visual token, CLS-weighted word quota; no-noun fallback to CLS attention.
Adaptive budget: No variable total K: fixed externally selected 192/128/64 (LLaVA-1.5) or 320 (NeXT). Allocates K_critical=floor(αK) and varying per-word shares K_j ∝ a_j, with α=0.3 default or 0.5 if K<100; variation across nouns is allocation within a fixed total, not adaptive per-sample token count.
Frozen components: All pretrained vision encoder, projector and decoder weights untouched.
Training objective: No differentiable loss. Heuristic maximize text-relevant critical evidence with CLS-weighted noun quotas under fixed K, and farthest-point diversity for remaining slots.
Benchmarks: MME; GQA; ScienceQA; POPE; TextVQA; VizWiz; VQAv2; MMBench; MM-Vet
Reported results: LLaVA-1.5-7B full 576 tokens: at 192 tokens CRISP 99.8% average normalized performance; 128 tokens 99.5%; 64 tokens 97.7%, with 9-benchmark Table I (PDF p. 4).; LLaVA-NeXT-7B full 2880 tokens: 320 tokens CRISP 96.9% mean normalized performance; POPE 88.2 vs full 86.5, TextVQA 58.9 vs full 64.9 (PDF p. 5, Table II).; 128-token LLaVA-1.5 ablation full MME 1794/MMB 62.8 vs removing Stage 1 1694/61.4 or Stage 2 1738/59.8 (PDF p. 5, Table III).; MME timing Table IV: LLaVA-1.5-7B 576→128 tokens, 8.47→2.46 TFLOPs, 318.6→94.6 MB KV, 22.0→45.0 decoded tok/s; full benchmark 2:21→1:35. NeXT 2880→320 tokens, 30.57→5.01 TFLOPs, 1084.7→190.6 MB KV, 18.4→40.4 tok/s, 4:29→1:56 (PDF p. 5).
Limitations: Budget K is externally fixed; no per-sample adequacy policy, cost/quality training or RL.; Computes every ViT patch; shared projected/text input space cosine might not reliably encode all answer dependencies.; Greedy diversity and noun-extraction overhead at inference; noun-free fallback loses query conditioning.; Reported speedups from decoder-only pruning cannot automatically be extended to full encoder/looped inference.
Warnings: Table I has baseline results from various implementations; figures should be attributed to CRISP evaluation, not directly comparable to SparseVLM’s own Table 1 (different measured baselines).; Only 320-token NeXT main comparison; 640-token row appears in the efficiency table, not the main benchmark comparison.

Paper title: GRIP-VLM: Group-Relative Importance Pruning for Efficient Vision-Language Models
Research category: Adaptive visual token compression; Token pruning and merging; Vision encoder post-training; Reinforcement learning for visual token optimization; Knowledge distillation
Primary contribution: Supervised scorer warm-up followed by GRPO over discrete keep/drop masks against task reward and token-equivalent budget; FiLM-modulated scorer takes current and target compression ratios and can plug between vision encoder/projector or inside decoder.
Training methodology: LLaVA-665K instruction tuning data; Adam 1e-5, 10 epochs, only scorer updated, all original LLM parameters frozen. Stage I L_scorer=L_distill+αL_KL+βL_ratio and budget curriculum; Stage II G=16 masks per instance, GRPO PPO-clipped objective with group-normalized advantage and KL to reference. Paper says backbone frozen for RL stage.
Compression mechanism: FiLM F_local_tilde=F_local⊙(1+γ)+β using target/current ratios; F_unique=F_local−masked mean; S_final=α S_learned+(1−α) S_heuristic. Stage I teacher full-token distillation; Stage II sample a_i~Bernoulli(p_i) and group-relative rewards for discrete mask trajectories.
Relevance to our proposal: Closest frozen-backbone RL pruning precedent, with vision-side or decoder-side scorer and budget-pressure conditioning. Novelty gap lies in explicit question dependence and endogenous per-sample token count in looped VLM.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: P0: strongest overlap on frozen backbone, vision-side scorer, GRPO and multiple budgets.
Method evidence (PDF pages): PDF p. 8, Fig. 5 and §4.1, Eqs. 4–5; PDF p. 9, §4.2, Eqs. 6–9; PDF p. 10, §5.1 (freeze/placement/hyperparameters); PDF p. 17, Appendix C
Experimental evidence (PDF pages): PDF p. 10, Table 1; PDF p. 11, Fig. 6, Table 2; PDF p. 12, Table 3; PDF p. 18, Table 4
Question conditioning: No explicit query embedding/cross-modal query alignment in scorer equations (local image feature, global image pool, target/current ratio, optional heuristic attention/norm). Decoder-side features may implicitly encode text, but encoder-side scorer is not established as explicitly question-conditioned.
Adaptive budget: FiLM adapts mask/scoring to externally specified target and current pruning ratio; curriculum spans equivalent budgets. This is cross-budget compatibility, not demonstrated sample-specific self-selected K. Table 1 tests preset K=192/128/64 of 576 on 7B and 176/110/55 on 13B.
Frozen components: All LLM parameters frozen throughout; method describes freezing VLM backbone for GRPO and only scorer optimized (PDF pp. 9–10). No original vision encoder/projector update reported.
Training objective: Stage I L_distill feature MSE + α KL(teacher/student logits)+β sparsity-ratio penalty (Eq. 6). Stage II J=E[(1/G)Σ_j min(ρ_j Â_j,clip(ρ_j,1±ε)Â_j)−β KL(πθ//πref)] (Eq. 7), Â_j=(r_j−group mean)/group std, r_j=R_task−γ max(0,T_eq−T_target) (Eq. 8); R_task binary correctness for verifiable tasks or 1−sigmoid(α(L−L_ref)) for open generation (Eq. 9).
Benchmarks: MME; POPE; ScienceQA; TextVQA; AI2D; GQA; MMBench-EN; OCRBench
Reported results: 7B Table 1 at 192 tokens: decoder+RL 100.22% normalized 8-benchmark average vs encoder+RL 98.47% and full 100%; 128 tokens decoder+RL 98.22% vs encoder+RL 97.12%; 64 tokens decoder+RL 90.71% vs encoder+RL 94.14%. At 64 tokens VisPruner 93.98% and DivPrune 93.76%, so decoder+RL is NOT best at that budget (PDF p. 10, Table 1).; 13B matched budgets: decoder+RL vs SparseVLM normalized averages 99.04 vs 98.12 at 176, 97.74 vs 96.32 at 110, 90.45 vs 87.36 at 55 (PDF p. 12, Table 3); individual metrics are not uniformly better, e.g. 110-token MME lower.; GQA TTFT table reports original 64.60 s, encoder+RL 43.20/38.40/36.40 s and decoder+RL 47.50/45.20/44.60 s at 192/128/64 respectively; paper describes 1.79× speedup at 64 and 15% faster at equal accuracy (PDF pp. 11, 18, Fig. 6 and Table 4).; At 128-token decoder+RL: 98.22% normalized average, without budget modulator 97.56%, without hybrid reward 97.21%; at 64 tokens 90.71/89.44/90.27% (PDF p. 11, Table 2).
Limitations: Budget-aware is not budget-deciding: no explicit per-question target selection or minimum token stopping rule.; Encoder-side scorer runs after full ViT, so it does not save vision-encoder work.; Question conditioning unspecified beyond decoder hidden states; vision-side scorer input lacks explicit text in method.; RL uses 16 VLM evaluations per instance and a 665K training set, with unclear total training GPU-hour cost.; At 64 tokens encoder+RL is stronger than decoder+RL, and several baselines outperform decoder+RL; Table 1 conflicts with broad best-Pareto prose.
Warnings: Paper Table 4 labels 64.60, 36.40 as TTFT seconds on GQA; these may be dataset-aggregate rather than per-request: do not call them per-image latency.; Abstract says 15% faster at equal accuracy, but Fig. 6 is plotted trade-off and does not identify a unique matched pair in the table.; The phrase “arbitrary compression ratios” means tested budget-aware conditioning, not empirical adaptive per-example budget selection.

Paper title: Glance, then Select: Evidence-Tempered Visual Token Selection for Extremely Compressed Multimodal LLMs
Research category: Adaptive visual token compression; Question-conditioned vision encoding; Token pruning and merging; Vision encoder post-training; Supervised and differentiable compression; Knowledge distillation
Primary contribution: One 1.9M-parameter question-conditioned evidence scorer routes a two-pass coarse-to-fine vision encoder and biases a diversity-based fixed-K visual token selector; standalone scorer can be trained with MLLM frozen, while strongest pipeline self-distills both encoder and decoder.
Training methodology: Scorer: freeze entire MLLM, supervise with listwise CE −Σ_i y_i log p_i where y_i normalized evidence-box coverage; AdamW 3e-4, batch 16, three epochs on 60K sampled images from 422K records (28K TextVQA, rest Visual-CoT). Strongest model: student vision encoder AND LLM trained on 14K prompts for 175 steps via one student rollout/prompt and token-level generalized JSD (α=0.5) on top-100 teacher/student logits plus tail; frozen dense full-token teacher, 256-token answer cap, 2e-6 ViT learning rate, 4.7 hours on 8 A800. Student trains using DivPrune, inference swaps in ETD.
Compression mechanism: Glance: quarter-sized patch grid + 25% evidence-high cells re-encoded at native resolution. ETD greedy chooses token maximizing d_i(Np_i)^0.25 where d_i=min_{j∈selected}(1−cos(x_i,x_j)); equal p gives DivPrune. Preserve original 2D token positions. Separate frozen-model evidence scorer and on-policy self-distillation of model.
Relevance to our proposal: High-threat latest evidence-conditioned visual compression with a frozen-decoder-compatible scorer-only variant, and supplementary variable per-image allocation. Biggest gap is trained endogenous K under frozen looped decoder and no box-label dependence.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: P0: same query-aware vision-side scorer and near-identical accuracy/efficiency motivation; explicitly tests budget allocation variant.
Method evidence (PDF pages): PDF pp. 3–5, §3, Eqs. 1–3 and Fig. 3; PDF p. 5, §3.5 (scorer/student training); PDF p. 23, Table S11 (allocation, supplement); PDF p. 21, Table S7 (box vs question ablation)
Experimental evidence (PDF pages): PDF p. 6, Table 1; PDF p. 7, Tables 2–3; PDF p. 23, Table S11; PDF p. 24, Table S12; PDF p. 26, Tables S14–S16
Question conditioning: Explicit: f_phi projects image features to 256-d, adds 2D positions, performs one cross-attention to projected question tokens, MLP on [h_i,c_i,h_i⊙mean(q)] yields softmax evidence p_i, used in both regional re-encoding and token selection. Trained with TextOCR aligned answer boxes and Visual-CoT evidence boxes.
Adaptive budget: Main tables strictly K=ceil(0.05N) for every image (or a separate floor-32 rule); varying N is not question-conditioned choice of K. Supplementary Table S11 explores fixed global budget redistribution fitted on training questions: K∝N^0.45, optionally ×2 for open prompts, while keeping dataset-average token budget; this is not main Glance-ETD pipeline or RL policy.
Frozen components: For scorer-only ETD, all pretrained MLLM parameters frozen. For headline Glance-ETD self-distillation, frozen full-token teacher but student vision encoder AND decoder/LLM trained: does NOT satisfy frozen target decoder. Scorer itself separately trained once with MLLM frozen.
Training objective: Scorer listwise CE on normalized box coverage, Eq. §3.3. Student token-level generalized Jensen–Shannon divergence α=0.5 to frozen full-token teacher along student-generated rollout, top-100 logits plus tail (§3.5). Teacher-KL Eq. 3 is a diagnostic for selecting γ=0.25, not training objective for scorer. ETD ranking Eq. 2 with fixed K. Supplementary global allocation rule K∝N^0.45·2^[open] is train-fitted, not learned online action.
Benchmarks: V*; HR-Bench 4K; GQA; MMMU; MMBench; MME; POPE; TextVQA; OCRBench; HR-Bench 8K; MME-RealWorld; HRScene; DocVQA; InfoVQA
Reported results: Qwen3.5-4B strict 5%/14 benchmark Ret.All: untrained DivPrune 71.3%; frozen-MLLM scorer ETD 82.0%; self-distilled DivPrune 85.6±0.2%; self-distilled dense+ETD 90.5±0.4%; Glance-ETD 91.6±0.3%. OCRBench Glance-ETD 590 vs full 848; TextVQA 76.3 vs full 80.5 (PDF p. 6, Table 1).; Gemma 4 E4B-it strict 5%/14: frozen ETD 78.6%; self-distilled dense ETD 84.2±0.7%; Glance-ETD 83.6±1.4%, so glance is NOT universally more accurate than dense ETD (PDF p. 6, Table 1).; Qwen nine-benchmark ablation (one seed) 10× encoder LR + dense DivPrune 88.8%; dense ETD 92.5%; glance ETD 93.3%. Glance stage cuts HR-Bench 4K ViT+LLM prefill 373→65 TFLOPs relative to dense models with same 5% selector (PDF p. 7, Table 2).; Qwen HR-Bench 4K one A800 bf16 median: full TTFT 4035 ms; dense ETD 3355 ms; Glance-ETD 1290 ms (3.13×); E2E 4329→1588 ms (2.73×), prefill TFLOPs 482→65 and batch-8 throughput 0.276→0.698 questions/s (PDF p. 26, Table S14).; Supplemental LT-OPD-model global allocation with ETD: at matched strict 5% aggregate budget, fixed same ratio/image retention 89.6%, K∝N^0.45 yields 94.6%, K∝N^0.45·2^[open] 95.1%; at floor-32 7.1% aggregate budget 95.9/96.3/97.3 respectively (PDF p. 23, Table S11).; Evidence perturbation: Qwen glance-model nine-benchmark retention ETD with true question 92.9%, wrong question 90.7%, no evidence/DivPrune 89.3% (PDF p. 24, Table S12).
Limitations: Strongest variant updates LLM decoder, so not frozen decoder training.; Primary token count fixed proportional to image patch count; no online task-specific adaptive budget, no RL selector.; Scorer uses supervised bounding-box annotations, 422K source records, separate training; possible data overlap with test images acknowledged (105 of 1284 DocVQA images), with exclusion control in supplement.; On smaller images glance path is skipped and pruning can slow TTFT; Table S15 gives TextVQA ~0.89× and GQA ~0.88× Glance-ETD TTFT speedup (PDF p. 26).; Suppl. S11 adaptive allocator fitted from training diagnostics and open-question type; must not present as deployed headline policy.
Warnings: Headline +17.3 points is against retrained LT-OPD without merge at 74.3%; released LT-OPD with merge retains 80.5%, a different comparison explicitly disclosed by authors (PDF pp. 2, 7, 16).; 91.6±0.3 is 14-benchmark three-seed mean; 93.3±0.4 is nine-benchmark three-seed mean, not interchangeable (PDF pp. 6–7).; Table S14 3.13× TTFT was timed with scorer-selected cells per caption, while Table S16 2.90× row was timed using diversity-selected cells; do not merge their timings.

Paper title: Hierarchical and Query-Aware Visual Token Pruning for High-Resolution LVLMs
Research category: Adaptive visual token compression; Question-conditioned vision encoding; Token pruning and merging; Adaptive computation and reasoning depth
Primary contribution: Three-level hierarchy budgets each image by thumbnail visual diversity, allocates across crops by CLIP crop/question similarity, then selects each crop’s tokens using z-scored projected-image/LLM-text embedding similarities plus global/local CLS visual attention.
Training methodology: Training-free plug-in; no parameter updates, no RL. Dataset-level population statistics and κ estimated from evaluation benchmark for mean-budget calibration.
Compression mechanism: Global thumbnail CLS top-floor(PR_j); crop CLIP CLS/EOS semantic relevance distributes remaining budget; token S=normalized(E)normalized(V)^T cosine, row-wise z-score over valid positions then q_{i,p}=max_t z(S_t)_p. Local score βz(local CLS)+(1−β)z(query), final α(global interpolated CLS normalized)+(1−α)(local normalized), per-crop top-b_i. Default α=0.7, β=0.5.
Relevance to our proposal: Most direct threat to combining pre-LLM question-conditioned visual token selection with variable per-sample total count and frozen pretrained decoder; decisive distinction is query-conditioned *count* and learned vision-side RL rather than dataset-calibrated image-only heuristic.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: P0: already has hierarchy of adaptive sample budget + query-aware crop/token allocation with frozen decoder.
Method evidence (PDF pages): PDF pp. 2–3, Fig. 3 and §III.A–C, Eqs. 1–3; PDF p. 4, Algorithm 1 and §III.D–E, Eqs. 4–8; PDF p. 4, §IV.A (hyperparameters and padded-budget definition)
Experimental evidence (PDF pages): PDF p. 2, Fig. 2; PDF p. 5, Tables I–IV; PDF p. 6, Table V and §IV.D
Question conditioning: Yes for crop budgets (cosine CLIP crop CLS and query text EOS) and token ranking (z-score cosine of projected image tokens versus each LLM query token embedding, max across query tokens). But total instance budget depends ONLY on image thumbnail diversity, not question.
Adaptive budget: H_j is a thumbnail-feature diversity measure, smaller when normalized thumbnail visual tokens point in similar directions (Eq. 1); R_j=clip(κR exp((H_j−μ_H)/(σ_HT_s)),R_min,R_max), with κ calibrated so benchmark mean R_j=R; default T_s=10, bounds [0.72R,2R]. Crop ratios r_i=min{R_j(1+π_i−1/n),1}, π=softmax(c/τ), τ=0.01; total baseline R=25% or 10% of 2880 padded positions. Dataset-wide μ_H,σ_H,κ imply transductive evaluation-set calibration or need deployment calibration.
Frozen components: All pretrained CLIP vision/text encoders, projector, LLM decoder unchanged; extra CLIP text query encoding and selection logic invoked at inference.
Training objective: No learned loss. Heuristic complexity-calibrated R_j budget Eq. 1–2, CLIP-softmax crop allocation Eq. 3, per-query-token z-score/cosine score Eqs. 4–5, CLS/query fusion Eqs. 6–8; benchmark-average retention constrained to R.
Benchmarks: VizWiz; GQA; ScienceQA-IMG; TextVQA; MME-Perception; MMBench; AI2D; POPE
Reported results: LLaVA-NeXT-7B 8-benchmark normalized avg: at R=25%, full 100%, HERO 97.8%, proposed fixed-per-image R 97.8%, proposed adaptive R_j 98.0%; at R=10%, HERO/HiRED 94.1%, fixed 94.6%, adaptive 94.8% (PDF p. 5, Table I).; At R=25% POPE 88.3 vs unpruned 87.6; GQA 63.0 vs 64.3; TextVQA 59.4 vs 61.4; MME-P 1514.1 vs 1519.3. At R=10% POPE 87.8, GQA 59.4, TextVQA 58.1 (PDF p. 5, Table I).; Sample-level qualitative allocations on POPE: 516/2880 tokens on snow scene vs 860/2880 on cluttered baseball scene (PDF p. 2, Fig. 2).; At R=25% ablation fixed R vs adaptive: MME-P 1501.4→1514.1 and AI2D 63.4→63.7; without query-score but adaptive: MME-P 1506.5, AI2D 63.6 (PDF p. 5, Table II).; POPE batch-1 RTX 4090 at R=25%: baseline 32.78 LLM-prefill TFLOPs, 16.55 GB peak, 3.15 q/s; adaptive method 10.88 TFLOPs, 14.84 GB, 6.35 q/s vs HERO 4.87 q/s (PDF pp. 4, 6, Table V).
Limitations: Per-instance count is image-complexity driven and independent of the question; query guides allocation/selection only.; Dataset-wide mean/SD and global κ calibrated over all M evaluation samples: not standalone online per-sample budget policy as described.; Only LLaVA-NeXT-7B tested; high-res multi-crop-specific pipeline plus extra CLIP text encoder.; ViT processes full original image/crops; stated TFLOPs are LLM prefill, not total cost.; Gain of adaptive over fixed R is only +0.2 normalized points on each average in Table I; no learned/RL or looped-decoder validation.
Warnings: R denominators include padded positions in a 2880-position LLaVA-NeXT baseline; reported ratios need care against methods counting valid tokens only.; Baseline rows without ∗ copied from GlobalCom2; ∗ re-run with released code, not a single uniform reproduction (PDF p. 5 Table I caption).; Full vision encoder cost omitted from Table V TFLOPs (explicitly LLM prefill); 2.0× is observed throughput, not total FLOPs reduction.

Paper title: MVP: Multi-View-Guided Token Pruning for Vision-Language Models
Research category: Adaptive visual token compression; Question-conditioned vision encoding; Token pruning and merging; Vision encoder post-training; Supervised and differentiable compression; Knowledge distillation
Primary contribution: MVP-PruneSet gathers success/failure labels from complementary pruning families; MVP-Pruner distills their evidence into a question-aware scorer, with an appendix experiment replacing fixed top-K by a global threshold for variable per-input count.
Training methodology: 56,192 image-question pairs filtered from GQA, OCR-VQA and TextVQA-related data (replace descriptive TextVQA subset with TextVQA training split; exclude text-only-solvable examples); loss L=L_rank+L_budget. Valid pairs have y_i-y_j>delta; soft-margin softplus((m-(s_i-s_j))/tau), coarse weighted by label gap with m=gamma*gap, fine inversely weighted by gap with m=mu, lambda_c=.3/lambda_f=.7. Budget BCEWithLogits(s, top-K(y)); delta=.02, gamma=4, mu=.1, tau=1. Distinct selectors/operating points not clarified; no RL.
Compression mechanism: Collect five masks/sample: GRASP variable-size and VisPruner/SCOPE at K=64,128. Evaluate each on frozen VLM for correctness. Within-family evidence efficiency E_m=Acc_m/R_m weights masks; normalize family weights, aggregate positive P_i=sum_f beta_f p_f,i and failed-mask Q_i=sum_f beta_f q_f,i; soft label y_i=P_i[1-Q_i(1-P_i)]. Select top-K of pruner logits at inference.
Relevance to our proposal: Very high: frozen decoder, trainable vision-side question-aware selector, explicit appendix threshold-count experiment; strong baseline and important novelty collision for adaptive count claims.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: A proposed method cannot claim novelty merely from question-conditioned vision-side training or threshold-derived per-example counts; needs calibrated budget/reward and loop-aware constraints with explicit comparison to MVP fixed and global-threshold variants.
Method evidence (PDF pages): PDF pp.4-6 (Secs.4.1-4.2, Eqs.1-8, Fig.5); p.9 (Limitations); p.13-14 (Appendix C.1, Table 6).
Experimental evidence (PDF pages): PDF p.7 Table 1, p.8 Table 2/Fig.6, pp.13-14 Tables 4-8.
Question conditioning: Explicit question-token cross-attention in pruner; GRASP's question-guided segmentation supplies offline teacher masks. Same image produces different selected patches for different questions (Fig. 8).
Adaptive budget: Main experiments use externally prescribed K=192/128/64 or fixed ratios. Appendix C.1/Table 6 tests a single global score threshold tau=0.3: per-sample count varies, mean 63.7 tokens and 94.42% normalized score versus 96.38% with fixed K=64; TextVQA falls from 56.3 to 43.6. Authors acknowledge scores rank relative importance and are not calibrated absolute necessity. Thus do NOT call this a validated learned budget controller, but do not claim the paper never tests adaptive counts.
Frozen components: Vision encoder, multimodal projector and language decoder/VLM remain frozen; only MVP-Pruner trained. Offline Qwen3-VL and SAM3 used for GRASP annotations, not tuned as part of inference.
Training objective: Supervised token-ranking/distillation and budget-level BCE, NOT downstream-reward RL; optimize relative token importance under fixed top-K labels.
Benchmarks: LLaVA-1.5-7B: GQA, MME, POPE, ScienceQA, TextVQA, SEED, VizWiz, VQAv2; Qwen2.5-VL-7B: GQA, MME, SEED, TextVQA, ScienceQA
Reported results: LLaVA Table 1: normalized averages 99.03% at 192, 98.39% at 128, 96.38% at 64/576; at 192 the fine-tuned VisionZip row is 99.14%, above MVP. Qwen Table 2: 95.88% at 30% keep and 91.74% at 20%, vs VisionZip 94.97/88.91%. Appendix Table 7 Qwen 20%: 118.41 to 89.22 ms, 1.33x, mean visual tokens 867.59 to 173.85. Appendix Table 6 global-threshold adaptive count 63.7 and 94.42% versus fixed-64 96.38%; TextVQA 43.6 versus 56.3. Appendix Table 8 annotation construction 20.7 GPU-hours (12.0 GRASP).
Limitations: Fixed main-study budget, threshold test has substantial OCR/TextVQA degradation; no RL, no looped decoder or repeated feedback; labeling requires offline multi-pruner runs, frozen-model correctness and auxiliary grounding/segmentation; evaluated two backbone families.
Warnings: Appendix C.1 contradicts any categorical assertion of no adaptive-budget experiment, even though main limitation says fixed K.; Main LLaVA 192-token MVP 99.03% is below fine-tuned VisionZip 99.14% in Table 1.; MVP-PruneSet is generated with downstream correctness but learned objective is supervised labels, not RL.

Paper title: ReDiPrune: Relevance-Diversity Pre-Projection Token Pruning for Efficient Multimodal LLMs
Research category: Adaptive visual token compression; Question-conditioned vision encoding; Token pruning and merging
Primary contribution: Training-free question-relevance plus max-min visual-diversity greedy selection in raw encoder features before projector, especially on video frames.
Training methodology: None: training-free heuristic; alpha, r, tau, M tuned as inference hyperparameters; no reward or policy gradients.
Compression mechanism: D_ij=1-cos(x_i,x_j); conceptual objective max_/S/=k [min_{i!=j in S}D_ij+alpha sum_{i in S}s_i]. Start with max relevance; choose next argmax_i[min_{u in S}D_ui+alpha s_i]. Optional relevance threshold and top-min(M_n,beta*k_n) candidate filter with beta=3, fallback top-M_n if too few; restore selected original order.
Relevance to our proposal: High as an explicit frozen-backbone vision-side query-conditioned pre-projector baseline, but not adaptive budget or RL.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: A question-aware vision-side score or relevance-plus-diversity fusion is prior art; differentiate via per-question budget learning and loop-aware RL, and benchmark against this training-free fixed-ratio approach.
Question conditioning: Explicit: q=sum_j w_j e_j, normalize/project to vision feature dimension; relevance s_i=cos(x_i,q). Tested average, middle-peak, self-attention and exponential word weighting; default tau=0 candidate prefilter (tau here is relevance threshold, not budget-control threshold).
Adaptive budget: No. k_n=max(1,round(r L_n)) separately per frame, prescribed ratio r. Candidate prefilter threshold tau and candidate cap M change eligibility, not the final retained count; r is fixed externally, though original frame length can vary.
Frozen components: All existing vision encoder, projector, and language model weights unchanged/frozen; no new trainable model reported.
Training objective: Inference-time heuristic relevance/diversity subset selection under fixed per-frame cardinality; not task-output reward optimization.
Benchmarks: Video-LLaVA-7B and LLaVA-NeXT-Video-7B: NExT-QA, EgoSchema, ActivityNet-QA, Video-ChatGPT; LLaVA-1.5-7B image: GQA, MMBench, MME, POPE, ScienceQA-IMG
Reported results: Table 1: LLaVA-NeXT-Video at 15% keep EgoSchema 45.6 vs 43.6 original, NExT-QA WUPS 26.42 vs 26.33; TFLOPs 29.918 to 4.429. Video-LLaVA at 10% ActivityNet-QA 45.69/3.40 vs original 42.73/3.33, TFLOPs 11.606 to 1.174. Image Table 2 58/576 tokens: GQA 57.62, MME 1392.90, POPE F1 85.39 vs dense 61.9/1506.5/85.9. Table 3 Video-LLaVA ActivityNet E2E 0.447 to 0.146 s and LLaVA-NeXT-Video 0.526 to 0.205 s; diversity-only DivPrune is faster (0.124/0.163 s).
Limitations: Hand-set per-frame ratio, no adaptive number or learned feedback, frame-local rather than global temporal allocation, evaluated LLaVA-style backbones; O(L_n^2 C_v) pairwise distances and greedy overhead; vision encoder cost unchanged.
Warnings: Fixed per-frame k_n despite its relevance candidate threshold: do not misclassify as adaptive budget.; PDF abstract says four video and five image benchmarks; introduction p.2 says six video and five image; experiment p.5 lists four video.; Image Table 2 does not universally beat every baseline: DART MMB 60.90 vs ReDiPrune 59.88; PruMerge+ larger 230-token budget; p.7 prose overstates 'best on all five'.

Paper title: Rescuing Your Pruning: Rethinking Visual Token Pruning and Post-Training Recovery in MLLMs
Research category: Adaptive visual token compression; Token pruning and merging
Primary contribution: Systematic 36-configuration study of fixed dropping/merging rules at encoder, projector and LLM with compression-aware post-training (CAPT), plus joint-stage search and TTFT measurements.
Training methodology: 282,293 single-turn samples from LLaVA-Icons plus OCR, chart, grounding and reasoning mixtures; one epoch, lr 1e-5, bf16, max length 8192, ZeRO-2, ~4h on eight H20 80GB per run; 36 single-stage configurations plus joint search. Gradients cut at discrete pruning criterion; weights upstream and downstream adapt.
Compression mechanism: Selection is fixed arithmetic and stop-gradient; re-pack variable-length sequences with padding/mask, preserve old position indices and recompute rotary embedding. Decomposes gap into G_data=M(Data-only)-M(Free), G_adapt=M(Prune-aware)-M(Data-only), residual=M(Dense-PT)-M(Prune-aware); RR=(G_data+G_adapt)/(M(Dense-PT)-M(Free)).
Relevance to our proposal: High engineering control and caution: frozen-decoder proposal must compare quality and end-to-end latency honestly against CAPT and show improvement without unfreezing decoder.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Distinguishes recoverable representation mismatch from discarded visual evidence; supports measuring whole-model TTFT rather than citing decoder-FLOP reductions alone.
Method evidence (PDF pages): PDF pp.4-5 (Sec.3 protocol/training and evaluation); pp.7-8 (Sec.4.2, Eqs.1-5); pp.9-10 (Sec.5, joint-stage search).
Question conditioning: Not a newly learned query-conditioned policy. Some studied rules may use attention or token similarity, but paper's optimization is backbone adaptation to fixed pruning rules rather than question-to-budget mapping.
Adaptive budget: No learned sample-specific budget controller; 40%,20%,10% stage sweep and fixed search (E70, P10 etc.), compare average visual-token keep per decoder layer for dynamic resolution.
Frozen components: NOT frozen decoder training: LLM-level methods unfreeze only LM, all other methods unfreeze every model module, including decoder and vision components; pruning rule itself never trainable. Inference uses pruned adapted model.
Training objective: Compression-aware model post-training on multimodal instruction data, preserving fixed selection arithmetic; no RL policy/reward. Joint search imposes GRR>=100 and ATR>=85 relative to dense-free model.
Benchmarks: General: GQA, VQAv2, OK-VQA; Reasoning: ScienceQA, AI2D, POPE; OCR: TextVQA, DocVQA, OCRBench; Grounding: RefCOCO, RefCOCO+, RefCOCOg
Reported results: All 36 single-stage settings improve ATR after CAPT. Qwen encoder SAINT 10%: GRR 81.4->97.5, OCR 25.6->61.4, grounding 4.0->64.8 (Table 1). Qwen projector AIM 10% after CAPT GRR 101.5, ATR 89.5. Qwen LLM PDrop 10% ATR 44.1->64.7; PACT 56.1->77.2 (Table 2). A100/SDPA batch 1, 5000 TextVQA examples: dense TTFT 213.06 ms, E70+P10 TTFT 138.61 ms (1.54x), LLM-stage 85.10->24.38 ms (3.49x), GRR 100.2, ATR 85.3 (Table 3); P10 alone TTFT 154.54 ms (1.38x).
Limitations: Does not meet frozen-decoder training constraint; one-epoch adaptation and fixed compression rules, no loop or RL; remaining OCR/grounding information loss, potential dense-free vs dense-post-trained comparison bias. Vision encoder accounts for 120.43/213.06 ms in measured Qwen TTFT, so pre-projector-only pruning need not improve TTFT much.
Warnings: Do not cite its gains as frozen-backbone gains: all but LLM-level modes train every module, including LM.; LLaVA-OV grounding >100% is relative to Dense-Free; paper notes Dense-PT reaches 150.3%, so cannot claim superiority to adapted dense.; TTFT timings use A100, SDPA, batch 1, resolution max_pixels=1,605,632; training uses 451,584 pixels; hardware/backends matter.

Paper title: StepPrune: Adaptive Sequential Visual Token Selection across Multimodal Large Language Models
Research category: Adaptive visual token compression; Question-conditioned vision encoding; Token pruning and merging; Vision encoder post-training; Supervised and differentiable compression; Adaptive computation and reasoning depth
Primary contribution: Conditional cross-modal pointer network selects complementary visual tokens sequentially and learns when to STOP, yielding query- and image-dependent count under a frozen vision tower/projector/LM; differentiable trajectory-based noise-gate training.
Training methodology: Frozen-VLM language-modeling loss on noise-gated tokens plus lambda*K/N, default lambda=.03, beta=.9, Tmax=288 for LLaVA-1.5; AdamW cosine LR 1e-5->1e-6, effective batch 16, one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell. Train cross-modal encoder/pointer/denoiser/text projection/START-STOP; no PPO/GRPO or environmental reward.
Compression mechanism: Pointer logits ell_t=PtrAttn(q_t,M)+selected-mask, p_t=softmax(ell_t/tau), hard argmax with straight-through e_a-sg(p)+p. Survival A_t=prod_{u<t}(1-p_u(STOP)); token trajectory score s_i=sum_{t<=Tmax} A_t p_t(i) beta^t, expected K=sum_t A_t(1-p_t(STOP)). SoftTopK polarizes scores with detached batch-mean expected K; variance-preserving gate x_tilde_i=sqrt(alpha_i)x_i+sqrt(1-alpha_i)epsilon_i and diagonal-only denoiser prevent leakage. Inference uses hard gathered subset, without gate/denoiser.
Relevance to our proposal: Extremely high: nearly entire target architecture (frozen decoder/projector, question-conditioned trainable vision-side selector, truly adaptive token count) is prior art; RL or loop-specific training must deliver separately measured gains and novel loop-aware state/reward.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Cannot claim question-conditioned per-input adaptive selection with frozen LLM as new. Use its explicit STOP, length regularizer, fixed-budget matched-mean controls, text-rich stress tests and selector-inclusive latency as essential baselines.
Method evidence (PDF pages): PDF pp.3-6 (Secs.3.1-3.5, Eqs.2-11 and Algorithm 1); p.7 (Sec.4.1 freezing and optimization).
Experimental evidence (PDF pages): PDF pp.7-10 (Secs.4.2-4.4, Tables 1-4, Fig.3); pp.12-13 (Tables 5-8 and limitations).
Question conditioning: Explicit E_text projected into vision space with gradual g_text gate, joint self-attention H=Enc([X;E_text]) and pointer decisions pi(a_t / selected history,X,Q).
Adaptive budget: Yes, learned STOP action on each pointer step sets K=T_stop-1, or groups of 5 for high-resolution; expected K=sum_t A_t(1-p_t(STOP)) under training and length penalty lambda*K/N. Per-input K varies even at matched test-set mean, but different global budget operating points train separate selectors. TextVQA mean 109.6 vs POPE 92.3 and MME 89.2; matched-mean adaptive vs fixed improves TextVQA +0.90pp and MME +0.81pp, harms ScienceQA -0.57pp and POPE -0.13pp.
Frozen components: Pretrained vision tower, multimodal projector AND language model frozen (Sec.3.4/4.1); only newly added selector-side modules trained.
Training objective: Differentiable language-model NLL/teacher-forced prediction plus explicit continuous expected-length regularization, NOT RL; hard selection optimized through surrogate straight-through and noise gating.
Benchmarks: LLaVA-1.5-7B: GQA, MMBench, MMBench-CN, MME, POPE, ScienceQA-IMG, VQAv2, TextVQA; Qwen2.5-VL-7B: MMBench, MME, POPE, ScienceQA-IMG, TextVQA; LLaVA-NeXT-7B: GQA, MMBench, MMBench-CN, MME, POPE, VQAv2, TextVQA; InternVL3-8B: TextVQA, MME, POPE, GQA, MMBench, MMBench-CN
Reported results: Table 1 LLaVA normalized mean 97.9/96.7/94.6% at mean K=192/128/64 from 576, with K=64 baseline VisionZip 92.0% and ApET 94.1%. Table 2 Qwen 97.8/95.0/90.9% at 66.7/77.8/88.9% pruning. Table 3 LLaVA-NeXT reports 98.7/95.8/90.2% at 77.8/88.9/94.4% pruning (NB conflicting narrative). Table 4 InternVL3 95.4% at 80% and 90.8% at 90%. Table 5 LLaVA K=64 prefill 59.95->40.05ms (1.50x), E2E 138.37->98.97ms; LLaVA-NeXT K=160 prefill 354.51->98.17ms (3.61x) but VisionZip is faster prefill 50.75ms. Fig.3 matched-mean adaptive-vs-fixed effects above.
Limitations: Not reinforcement learning, not a looped decoder; sequential selector latency rises with N and group-size trade-off weakens tokenwise history dependence; premature STOP misses fine local/OCR evidence; surrogate full-length training vs hard inference mismatch; budget operating points require distinct selectors; video/cross-backbone weight transfer not demonstrated.
Warnings: Sec.4.2 prose says LLaVA-NeXT retention 97.1/92.1/88.2%, while Table 3 reports 98.7/95.8/90.2% at the corresponding three pruning rates; Table 5 gives 92.1% for K=320 and 88.2% for K=160, apparently swapped/mismatched with Table 3. Preserve source-specific numbers rather than silently reconciling.; Table 5 LLaVA K=128 StepPrune prefill 50.08ms versus VisionZip 29.51ms; not universally faster than baselines.; Fig.3 matched-average adaptive budget helps four benchmarks but hurts two; per-example K is not automatically monotonic with semantic difficulty.

Paper title: TOP-RL: Task-Optimized Progressive Token Pruning with Reinforcement Learning for Large Vision Language Models
Research category: Adaptive visual token compression; Token pruning and merging; Reinforcement learning for visual token optimization; Adaptive computation and reasoning depth
Primary contribution: Multi-stage decoder-layer visual-token pruning as MDP with PPO, task-metric plus token-retention rewards, task/layer-dependent pruning analysis; trainable actor/critic around an otherwise inference-only LVLM.
Training methodology: Collect image-question/output episodes, score generated answer using task-specific metrics (paper names BLEU, accuracy etc.) and retention efficiency, PPO actor/critic. The PDF defers complete actor/critic architecture, training settings and ablations to an appendix not present in this nine-page supplied PDF; do not invent a specific learning rate or stage count.
Compression mechanism: MDP state s_t=[t,H_t^v], binary action mask m_t, next state transformer layers(mask,state); optimize expected sum_t gamma^(t-1)r_t, gamma=.9. Defines Q as task metric pruned/full and L_t as retained/original, stage objective Q-L_t; step reward r_t=r_Q-alpha_t*r_t^L with r_Q=Q_pruned/Q_full and r_t^L=L_t/L (PDF Eq.5 typography ambiguous), alpha_t=eta^(T-t), eta=.95 to favor early pruning. Reward computed after generation and assigned densely to pruning stages. PPO+GAE with fixed-shape attention masking G_ij=1 if i=j else mask_j for variable-length compatibility; train masks via Gumbel-softmax tau annealed 1.0->.05.
Relevance to our proposal: Critical RL-pruning prior art: end-task task-metric/retention reward plus PPO and progressive masking already claimed, but location differs from vision-side pre-LLM and per-question adaptive K.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Avoid claiming RL visual pruning or accuracy-minus-token reward is novel; demonstrate frozen-decoder, vision-side, question-explicit, loop-aware sample-specific budget and actual end-to-end gains against TOP-RL.
Method evidence (PDF pages): PDF pp.3-5 (Fig.3, Problem Formulation, Task-Optimized RL Analysis Eqs.1-7, RL implementation); p.5 notes complete settings deferred to unavailable Appendix A.
Experimental evidence (PDF pages): PDF pp.5-7 (Experiments, Tables 1-4 and cross-task transfer).
Question conditioning: Task-conditioned indirectly via task-specific QA/metric rewards and decoder visual states, which can carry prompt interactions; formal actor state in Sec. Task-Optimized RL Analysis is [stage, visual hidden states] and does not explicitly append raw question tokens or q. Cross-task transfer experiments train separate agents on different tasks, so do not conflate task-aware rewards with explicit per-question encoder-side policy input.
Adaptive budget: Reports mean retained count at prescribed operating points (e.g. average 192/64 LLaVA, average 320 NeXT) and variable masks, but describes deterministic TOP-K at inference; no learned STOP action or independently validated per-question learned cardinality. Agent adjusts stage-wise masks within token-ratio constraint.
Frozen components: Described as inference-only integration with pretrained LVLM; paper does not report retraining vision tower/projector/LM weights, only RL pruning agent. This is NOT vision-side-only: its masks intervene in decoder transformer layers.
Training objective: PPO maximizes task-metric retention minus stage-dependent surviving-token ratio (plus discounted trajectory), not language-modeling NLL or a learned per-question count at encoder output.
Benchmarks: LLaVA-1.5-7B: POPE, VizWiz, Flickr30k, RefCOCO, TextVQA, GQA, AI2D, MathVista, ScienceQA; Video-LLaVA: MSVD, MSRVTT, ActivityNet; LLaVA-NeXT-7B efficiency/F1; cross-task agent transfer: TextVQA, POPE, ScienceQA, GQA
Reported results: LLaVA-1.5 Table 1: mean score retention 97.6% at mean 192/576 tokens and 91.0% at mean 64/576; e.g. at 192 MathVista 23.0 vs dense 24.6. Video Table 2 2048->194 mean visual tokens, mean retention 93.9%. LLaVA-NeXT Table 3 at average 320 tokens: total time 28:21->14:48 (1.91x), 24.6->2.64 TFLOPs (9.32x), F1 91.6->87.2. Cross-task Table 4 transfer from TextVQA agent to SQA yields 46.4 vs SQA-trained 69.6, highlighting specialization.
Limitations: No demonstrated explicit raw-query input to actor, no pre-projector or vision-tower savings, per-task training and cross-task degradation, deterministic top-k contradicts treating output length as unconstrained learned variable; supplied PDF lacks promised appendix and training specifics. Its total-runtime speedup cannot be attributed solely to token count without baseline setup details.
Warnings: Eq.5 reward typesetting is garbled in extracted PDF and prose ambiguously says Q_p/L_p only after all steps while assigning stage-wise rewards; verify PDF typeset before literal formula reuse.; Paper calls dense signals fine-grained, but terminal output task metric appears reused at stages; distinguish from actual per-step intermediate task-delta rewards of TPRL.; Do not claim all decoder weights train; text says inference-only TOP-RL and actor/critic training.

Paper title: Language-Guided Token Compression with Reinforcement Learning in Large Vision-Language Models (TPRL)
Research category: Adaptive visual token compression; Question-conditioned vision encoding; Token pruning and merging; Reinforcement learning for visual token optimization; Adaptive computation and reasoning depth
Primary contribution: Query-conditioned PPO policy for visual-token pruning, token-wise autoencoder compact RL state, VisPruner demonstration pretraining and multistep training trajectories followed by one-shot pre-LLM threshold pruning.
Training methodology: Three phases: tokenwise reconstruction autoencoder; supervised BCE imitation on 50K VisPruner image-query trajectories with no mask->25% pruning->50% pruning; PPO fine-tuning with Tmax=3. Training data are all seven benchmark training splits. Sec.4.3 Table 5 compares a frozen LLM to fine-tuned LLM and reports the fine-tuned row higher, so main full-TPRL scores are not evidence that only vision-side modules were trained.
Compression mechanism: Tokenwise E minimizes L_rec=(1/N)sum_i//h_i-D(E(h_i))//^2 and is then frozen. Binary per-token mask at training step t: a_t,i ~ Bernoulli(lambda_disc^t*p_t,i), lambda_disc=.5; future states retain compressed codes only. r_t=alpha*(1/B)sum_b[Score(H_t^b,q^b)-Score(H_(t-1)^b,q^b)]+beta*(1/B)sum_b(1-K_t^b/K_(t-1)^b), alpha=1,beta=.1. PPO clipped actor + value MSE - entropy with GAE gamma=.99, lambda=.95; inference action 1[p_i>tau].
Relevance to our proposal: Most direct threat to novelty of question-conditioned adaptive RL visual token count: essentially this combination already exists. Frozen-decoder-only and loop-aware causal feedback, if substantiated, distinguish target from full fine-tuned model.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Do not claim first language-guided RL visual pruning or reward balancing score/compression. Benchmark against TPRL frozen-LLM Table 5 row, match mean K, and compare one-shot versus genuine loop-aware budget adaptation.
Method evidence (PDF pages): PDF pp.4-8 (Secs.3.1-3.5, Eqs.1-24 and inference protocol); p.9 (Sec.4.1 hyperparameters/threshold).
Experimental evidence (PDF pages): PDF pp.9-13 (Secs.4.1-4.3, Tables 1-8 incl. frozen-LLM ablation Table 5).
Question conditioning: Explicit state s_t=(Z_t,q) where q is query text embedding; policy/value share cross-modal attention on [Z_t;q_tilde]. Training answer-score changes for the same question supervise choices.
Adaptive budget: Yes in a limited sense: per-token output probabilities thresholded at inference yield varying per-example cardinality; thresholds tau=.55/.67/.74 calibrated to average 192/144/128 tokens on seven benchmarks. No explicit STOP/budget head or exact per-question minimum-necessary count; training has up to three pruning steps but inference is one-shot, NOT per-loop iterative pruning.
Frozen components: Autoencoder E is frozen after reconstruction; original visual encoder and projector are used as pretrained feature extractor, but full reported TPRL includes LLM fine-tuning according to Sec.4.3/Table 5 (frozen is an explicit lower-scoring ablation). Do NOT classify headline results as frozen-decoder proof.
Training objective: Actual end-task incremental score reward plus incremental compression reward for PPO, with supervised LfD warm start and reconstruction pretraining; contrast with TOP-RL's terminal metric broadcast to layer steps.
Benchmarks: LLaVA-1.5-7B: GQA, MMBench, MME, POPE, SEED-Bench, ScienceQA-Image, VQAv2; LLaVA-1.5-13B: GQA, MMBench, MME, POPE, ScienceQA-Image (paper prose also mentions SEED, but Table 2 omits it); Qwen2.5-VL-3B: GQA, MME, ScienceQA-Image, VQAv2
Reported results: LLaVA-1.5-7B Table 1: 576 dense, TPRL mean 192/144/128 tokens and average retention 99.3/98.4/97.7%; at 192 GQA 61.1 vs dense 62.0, MMBench 66.1 vs 64.6. Table 2 13B 192/128 mean normalized 99.2/97.1%. Table 3 Qwen-3B 144/128 mean normalized 98.1/97.7% vs 256 dense. Table 4 LLaVA-7B at 192 latency 57.8->26.7ms (53.8% reduction), FLOPs 9.6->4.4T (54.2% reduction), memory 302.4->100.9MB; FastV 192 is faster/less FLOPs but far lower accuracy. Table 5 192-token frozen vs fine-tuned relative scores: VQAv2 98.8 vs 99.6%, MMB 99.5 vs 102.3%, MME 98.5 vs 99.4%, POPE 98.6 vs 99.7%.
Limitations: Full reported setting fine-tunes language model; multi-step RL occurs during learning but inference is thresholded one-shot; threshold calibrated to target average budget rather than policy-learned STOP; per-token all-pairs self-attention policy overhead; text lacks looped decoder / repeated visual interaction; potential train/test task-family leakage concern requires careful split audit.
Warnings: Abstract's 'up to 66.7% tokens' conflicts with Tables 1-3 reporting 75-77.8% pruning on LLaVA and Table 3 Qwen baseline 256; do not quote abstract as maximum achieved reduction.; Sec.4.1 says 1024->64-dimensional autoencoder; p.11 discusses 4096->256 and says 128 is poor: dimension claims conflict, likely different feature stage/model; avoid one universal latent size.; Sec.4.1 prose maps tau=.55/.67/.74 to 192/144/128 averaged benchmarks, but Qwen original 256; quoted 66.7/75/77.8% ratios are LLaVA-576-specific.; Sec.4.1 prose claims 13B evaluation SEED, but Table 2 contains no SEED column.; Main full-model numbers must not be represented as frozen-decoder-only; Table 5 explicitly reports and favors fine-tuning.

Paper title: Visual Adversarial Examples Jailbreak Aligned Large Language Models
Primary contribution: Optimized image can broadly circumvent multimodal safety alignment.
Training methodology: 5000 PGD steps, batch 8 on 66 harmful sentences; no victim training.
Compression mechanism: PGD optimized pixels maximize harmful-corpus likelihood under bounded or unconstrained pixel constraint; universal downstream text prompts.
Relevance to our proposal: Safety ancillary: audit token-budget-dependent jailbreak/refusal behavior.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Visual image is a safety attack surface; no visual compression method.
Question conditioning: Universal attack optimized irrespective of downstream harmful question.
Adaptive budget: No.
Frozen components: Victim model weights frozen for attack-time image optimization.
Training objective: Minimize negative log-likelihood of harmful corpus, not utility/compute.
Benchmarks: 40 harmful instructions; RealToxicityPrompts; MiniGPT-4; InstructBLIP; LLaVA
Reported results: MiniGPT-4 Table 1: unconstrained image versus benign image ASR identity attack 78.5% vs 26.2%, disinformation 91.1% vs 48.9%, violence/crime 84.0% vs 50.1%.; RealToxicityPrompts challenging subset Perspective API Any toxicity 66.0±1.0% vs 34.8±1.6% (Table 2).
Limitations: Incomplete harm coverage; manual judgments have no universal standard, toxicity API imperfect (p.11).
Warnings: Attack success rate is undesirable; distinguish white-box attack and transfer.

Paper title: MM-SafetyBench: A Benchmark for Safety Evaluation of Multimodal Large Language Models
Primary contribution: 13-scenario safety benchmark with image-bearing unsafe phrases and safety-prompt mitigation.
Training methodology: Dataset construction and inference prompt only, no model training.
Compression mechanism: 1680 questions each with SD, typography, and combined image; GPT-4-aided safety judgments; prefix safety prompt.
Relevance to our proposal: Ancillary OCR/typography and safety metric for compression benchmarks.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Test visual safety retention across token budgets.
Question conditioning: Generated visual content tied to unsafe key phrase, not a question-aware visual compressor.
Adaptive budget: No.
Frozen components: All evaluated model parameters unchanged.

Benchmarks: MM-SafetyBench 5040 image-question pairs; tiny 504 pairs; 13 scenarios
Reported results: Default Table 3: LLaVA-1.5-7B mean ASR text-only 41.01%, typography 71.52%, combined 72.14%; 13B 44.55%, 72.15%, 72.91%.; Tiny Fig.6: safety prompt lowers LLaVA-1.5 ASR 77.33% to 15.68%.

Paper title: FigStep: Jailbreaking Large Vision-Language Models via Typographic Visual Prompts
Primary contribution: Renders prohibited list instruction in image and uses benign textual completion cue to breach visual-text safety.
Training methodology: Handcrafted gradient-free prompt attack with GPT paraphrasing; no model training.
Compression mechanism: Paraphrase harmful question into numbered heading image; neutral completion prompt; defense/ablation variants.
Relevance to our proposal: Safety stress test for OCR preservation/refusal under image compression.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Text-image safety can change with visual sampling resolution.
Question conditioning: Attack text image per harmful question, not token selection.
Adaptive budget: No.
Frozen components: Victim models frozen.

Benchmarks: SafeBench 500 harmful questions; SafeBench-Tiny 50; six LVLMs
Reported results: SafeBench Table 1 six open-source model mean ASR vanilla 44.80%, FigStep 82.50%; CogVLM 8.20%→87.00%.; Tiny manual ablation FigStep ASR LLaVA/MiniGPT-4/CogVLM 92/90/82% versus image-only 4/34/0% (Table 2).; GPT-4V Table 7 baseline 18%, FigStep 34%, FigStep-Pro 70% under reported repeated-query case study.

Paper title: BLIP-3: A Family of Open Large Multimodal Models
Research category: Multimodal alignment and connector design; Foundational and background literature
Primary contribution: Per-image-patch Perceiver compression; instruction-aware resampler ablation reports no significant gain.
Training methodology: Base 384² pretraining ~100B multimodal tokens, high-res pretraining, SFT, optional multi-image SFT.

Relevance to our proposal: Direct connector/token-compression baseline and negative result for naive question conditioning.

Reported results: Table 4 p.7 OCR aggregate rises 64.6→67.2 with large high-resolution Stage-2 grid while general VQA 63.5→63.3.; Fig.7 p.8: per-patch sampling beats fixed global sampling on OCR; instruction-aware query augmentation has no significant common-domain gain.

Paper title: Large Language Models are Strong Audio-Visual Speech Recognition Learners
Primary contribution: Llama-AVSR studies fixed K-fold grouping of audio/lip-video features before LLM and separate modality performance tradeoffs.
Training methodology: Train projectors and optional LoRA on 30/433h LRS3 and up to 1756h with pseudo-labeled VoxCeleb2.
Compression mechanism: Concatenate K consecutive temporal features along hidden dimension, two-layer projectors produce 1/K token sequence, concatenate with text.
Relevance to our proposal: Analogy for modality-sensitive token budget and noisy-input robustness.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Visual speech informative when audio noisy; token allocation across modalities matters.
Question conditioning: Fixed speech transcription instruction, no query-dependent compression.
Adaptive budget: K=1–5 manually selected per setup/modality, not learned per sample.
Frozen components: Encoders frozen except video LoRA option; LLM backbone frozen except optional LLM LoRA.
Training objective: Autoregressive transcription loss; WER/efficiency sweep, no joint compute objective.
Benchmarks: LRS3 ASR/VSR/AVSR; NOISEX noise
Reported results: p.4 §III: K=1→5 mean audio tokens 584→117; authors report small impact on ASR WER in sweep.; Table III p.4 -5 dB AVSR WER audio/video K=3/3:17.6%; K=4/2:16.9%; no-video 63.1%.
Limitations: Lip-ROI AVSR only; K optimizes WER not visual QA.
Warnings: Paper arXiv 2409.12319, PDF revision 2025; initial year 2024.

Paper title: LLaMA-Omni: Seamless Speech Interaction with Large Language Models

Training methodology: Speech instruction triplets InstructS2S-200K; two training stages for speech input/text then speech output.

Relevance to our proposal: Weak analogy for compute/quality control but not visual token allocation.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: No visual input.

Adaptive budget: Speech output chunk Ω controls latency/quality, not learned visual budget.

Reported results: Table 1 p.7 speech-to-text content score 3.23; speech-to-speech content 2.69; ASR-WER 11.61%.; Table 2 p.8 speech chunk Ω=10 latency 226.13ms and UTMOS 3.2304 vs Ω=∞ latency 1924.62ms and UTMOS 3.9296.

Warnings: Manifest filename LLava-Omni misleading: actual paper LLaMA-Omni, speech-only.

Paper title: MMS-LLaMA: Efficient LLM-based Audio-Visual Speech Recognition with Minimal Multimodal Speech Tokens
Primary contribution: Speech-rate-conditioned AV Q-Former allocates per-utterance query count and reduces LLM token/FLOP cost.

Relevance to our proposal: Closest conceptual budget-allocation prior in this batch, but adaptive to speech rate not visual question.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Use as dynamic learned query-count baseline/analogy with explicit FLOPs and modality effects.
Question conditioning: Input speech-rate-conditioned, not user-question-conditioned.
Adaptive budget: Yes; predictor scales allocated learnable queries per utterance duration and speaking rate.
Frozen components: Encoders, LLM text embedding and speech-rate predictor frozen in main stage; LLM receives LoRA.

Benchmarks: LRS3 ASR/AVSR/VSR; babble-noise SNR
Reported results: Abstract: ~3.5 tokens/s; 86% token reduction and 35.7% FLOP reduction versus previous multimodal speech LLM.; Table 2 p.7 baseline 25 tokens/s, 2.24T FLOPs, 18.2GB, clean WER 0.97%; early fusion 12.5 tokens/s, 1.81T, 14.7GB, WER 0.92%.; Table 1 p.6 LRS3 1759h noisy/clean WER 1.9%/0.72%.

Frozen components: LM frozen only initial adapter stage; final stage all weights unfrozen.

Benchmarks: LibriSpeech WER; qualitative streamed conversations
Reported results: Table 2 p.7 Mini-Omni LibriSpeech test-clean/test-other WER 4.5%/9.7%, versus Whisper-small 3.4%/7.6%.; Paper §4.4 provides speech streaming qualitative examples; no systematic visual benchmark or loop cost.

Relevance to our proposal: Indirect multimodal training interference caution for modifying pretrained VLM.

Adaptive budget: No.

Paper title: Ola: Pushing the Frontiers of Omni-Modal Language Model with Progressive Modality Alignment
Research category: Multimodal alignment and connector design; Foundational and background literature
Primary contribution: Progressive image→video→audio alignment and local-global attention pooling for visual token downsampling.
Training methodology: Progressive image-text, text-video, then vision-audio; image MLP alignment and multimodal SFT, 10× fixed audio downsampling.
Compression mechanism: 2× bilinear spatial pooling generates global features, concat with local features, softmax MLP predicts regional importance weights, weighted local-global pooled visual representations.
Relevance to our proposal: Direct spatial compression architectural baseline and cross-modal preservation test.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Content-weighted local/global pooling could be adapted to query-guided budget under frozen decoder.
Question conditioning: Pooling scores local visual/global features, not user question.
Adaptive budget: Fixed 2× spatial pooling; content-dependent importance weights but not adaptive token count or per-question budget.
Frozen components: Not frozen decoder; staged pretraining/SFT updates model; source vision encoder initialized from SigLIP and fine-tuned.
Training objective: Modality alignment and supervised multimodal instruction loss; no explicit FLOP/loop penalty.
Benchmarks: MMBench; MMMU; MMStar; VideoMME; OCRBench; LibriSpeech; AIR-Bench
Reported results: Table 1 p.6 Ola MMBench-1.1 84.3, MMMU 57.0, VideoMME no-sub 68.4, LibriSpeech test-clean WER 1.9.; Table 3 p.8 VideoMME overall 63.8 before omni stage vs 68.4 after adding video-audio training in reported variant; Table 5/§4.3 checks retained image performance.
Limitations: Full omni model training rather than frozen decoder; pooling loses resolution; externally sourced TTS, no per-question token policy.
Warnings: Visual pooling produces fixed grid size, not adaptive budget.

Paper title: Qwen2.5-Omni Technical Report
Primary contribution: Thinker–Talker multimodal model with blockwise audio/video encoding, time-aligned RoPE, streaming text/speech.

Relevance to our proposal: Potential pretrained multimodal backbone / multi-modality evaluation; not compression prior.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Compare modality-specific retention in future budget policy.
Question conditioning: Multimodal questions processed by Thinker but visual frame-rate selected for temporal alignment, not question-specific.

Paper title: Qwen3-Omni Technical Report
Primary contribution: Thinker/Talker MoE with audio-video streaming and non-degradation evaluations across modalities, not a visual compressor.
Training methodology: Large multimodal pretraining, SFT/distillation (off/on-policy KL), GSPO posttraining across modalities.
Compression mechanism: Time-aligned multimodal RoPE, asynchronous Talker prefill, residual-codebook speech streaming; MoE throughput optimization.
Relevance to our proposal: Possible compute/throughput architecture baseline and retention across modalities, not token compression.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Shows model-scale and modality retention concerns for any compression intervention.
Question conditioning: Model answers queries, no query-conditioned visual budget.
Adaptive budget: Dynamic video sampling/frame rate, not learned per-question vision token count.
Frozen components: End-to-end training, not frozen decoder.
Training objective: Generative learning, distillation KL, policy optimization; serving latency measured, no visual-budget/loop joint objective.
Benchmarks: MMMU-Pro; MathVista; ChartQA; WorldSense; DailyOmni; VoiceBench; ASR
Reported results: Table 1 p.6 reports end-to-end first packet latency audio/video 234/547 ms for Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B.; Table 9 p.12 Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct MMMU-Prooverall 57.0 and MathVista mini 75.9 (check named model column); Table 11 p.13 WorldSense 54.0 (same model).; §5.1 p.12 explicitly notes weak long-video due to limited positional extrapolation/context.
Limitations: Paper explicitly reports suboptimal long-video due to position extrapolation and context restrictions (§5.1.3).
Warnings: Qwen3-Omni model variant matters (Instruct/Thinking/Flash); figures are paper-reported, not current product claims.

Paper title: VITA-1.5: Towards GPT-4o Level Real-Time Vision and Speech Interaction
Primary contribution: Multi-stage vision→audio-input→audio-output training retains visual capability; visual encoder 256 tokens/image and dynamic tiling.
Training methodology: Stage 1.1 trains visual adapter only with encoder/LLM frozen; stages 1.2/1.3 train vision encoder/adapter/LLM; audio input stage trains multimodal modules and audio output stage freezes LLM.
Compression mechanism: High-resolution dynamic image tiling; video samples 4–16 frames and deliberately omits dynamic tiling for video to avoid excess tokens.
Relevance to our proposal: Frozen visual-adapter stage and modality-retention evidence; relevant to frozen decoder feasibility but no adaptive visual compression.
Reason for inclusion or exclusion: Stage-wise training helps isolate changes, and OCR-sensitive high-resolution detail matters.
Question conditioning: Image/video question at decoder; tiling/frame count based on resolution/duration, not question.
Adaptive budget: Duration-based video frame counts; fixed 256 tokens per frame, no query-specific budget.
Frozen components: LLM and visual encoder frozen only initial visual adapter alignment stage; LLM trainable subsequent visual/audio stages; LLM frozen final speech output stage.
Training objective: Caption/QA supervised generation, CTC audio encoder and text/speech decoder losses, not token/loop penalty.
Benchmarks: MMBench; MMStar; MMMU; MathVista; OCRBench; Video-MME; LibriSpeech
Reported results: Table 2 p.7 image aggregate 67.1 Stage 1 to 66.8 Stage 3; OCRBench 752→732, showing small aggregate but specific OCR regression.; Table 3 p.8 Video-MME no-sub 56.8 Stage 1 vs 56.1 Stage 3; Table 4 p.8 LibriSpeech test-clean/test-other WER 3.4/7.5.
Limitations: Visual OCR and Video-MME mildly regress after audio; no joint compute policy; duration-based frame cap may discard detail.
Warnings: Manifest Vita-01 names same VITA-1.5 PDF as id76. PDF states 110,000h internal speech data but Stage 2.1 specifies 11,000h subset; do not conflate.
